Let the angle bisectors of $\angle BAC$ and $\angle MON$ meet at $R$. Show that the circumcircles of triangles $BMR$ and $CNR$ intersect at a point on segment $BC$.

style.text: Let $\triangle XYZ$ be an acute-angled triangle with $XY \neq XZ$. The circle with diameter $YZ$ intersects the sides $XY$ and $XZ$ at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. Denote by $W$ the midpoint of the side $YZ$. The bisectors of the angles $YXZ$ and $PWQ$ intersect at $S$. Prove that the circumcircles of the triangles $YPS$ and $ZQS$ have a common point lying on the side $YZ$.

exact.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers, show that} \quad 1 < \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{y^2 + z^2}} + \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2 + x^2}} \le \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.

paraphrase.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Show that} \quad 1 < \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{y^2 + z^2}} + \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2 + x^2}} \le \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.

style.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that} \quad 1 < \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{y^2 + z^2}} + \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2 + x^2}} \le \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.

exact.text: Let $A_1B_1C_1 - ABC$ be a right triangular prism where $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$ and $AB = AC = AA_1 = 1$. Define $G$ and $E$ as the midpoints of $A_1B_1$ and $CC_1$, respectively. If $MS \perp NT$, find the possible values of the length $ST$.

style.text: Consider a rectangular box $P_1Q_1R_1 - PQR$ with $\angle QPR = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $PQ = PR = PP_1 = 1$. Let $M, N$ be the midpoints of $P_1Q_1$, $RR_1$ respectively; and $X, Y$ be variable points on segments $PR, PQ$ (not including endpoints). If $MX \perp NY$, determine the range of the length of $XY$.

exact.text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be real numbers such that $x + y + z = 3$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{5x^2 - 4x + 11} + \frac{1}{5y^2 - 4y + 11} + \frac{1}{5z^2 - 4z + 11} \le \frac{1}{4}.
$$

$$

\frac{1}{5x^2 - 4x + 11} + \frac{1}{5y^2 - 4y + 11} + \frac{1}{5z^2 - 4z + 11} \le \frac{1}{4}.

exact.text: Prove the following statements: (1) If $2k - 1$ is a prime number, then for any set of distinct positive integers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_k$ there exist $i, j \in \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ such that $\frac{b_i + b_j}{\gcd(b_i, b_j)} \ge 2k - 1$. (2) If $2k - 1$ is a composite number, then there exists a set of distinct positive integers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_k$ such that $\frac{b_i + b_j}{\gcd(b_i, b_j)} < 2k - 1$ for all $i, j \in \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$. Here $\gcd(x, y)$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $x$ and $y$.

paraphrase.text:
Prove the following statements:

(1) If $2n-1$ is a prime number, then for any set of $n$ distinct positive integers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$, there exist $i, j$ with $1 \le i, j \le n$ such that $\frac{b_i + b_j}{\gcd(b_i, b_j)} \ge 2n-1$.

(2) If $2n-1$ is a composite number, then there exists a set of $n$ distinct positive integers $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ such that $\frac{b_i + b_j}{\gcd(b_i, b_j)} < 2n-1$ for all $i, j$ with $1 \le i, j \le n$.

style.text:
Let $p = 2n-1$. Prove that:

(1) If $p$ is a prime, then for any set of $n$ distinct positive integers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$, there exist $i \ne j$ such that $\frac{x_i + x_j}{\gcd(x_i, x_j)} \ge p$.

(2) If $p$ is composite, then there exists a set of $n$ distinct positive integers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ such that for all $i \ne j$, $\frac{x_i + x_j}{\gcd(x_i, x_j)} < p$.

exact.text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be nonnegative real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. Show that
$$
\sqrt{x + \frac{(y - z)^2}{4}} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z} \le \sqrt{3}.
$$

paraphrase.text:
Given nonnegative real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ satisfying $x + y + z = 1$, show that
$$
\sqrt{x + \frac{(y-z)^2}{4}} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z} \le \sqrt{3}.
$$

style.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \ge 0 \text{ with } x + y + z = 1. \text{ Show that} \quad \sqrt{x + \frac{(y-z)^2}{4}} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z} \le \sqrt{3}.

exact.text: Let $b_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{(n+1-k)k}$. Prove that $b_{n+1} < b_n$ for $n \ge 2$.

paraphrase.text: Let $b_n = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \frac{1}{m(n+1-m)}$. Prove that $b_{n+1} < b_n$ for $n \ge 2$.

style.text: Let $b_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{k(n-k+1)}$. Prove that $b_{n+1} < b_n$ for $n \ge 2$.

exact.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and $f(n)$ denote the number of sequences $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ with $a_i \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ such that: (i) $a_i \neq a_{i+1}$ for all $i = 1, 2, \dots, n-1$; (ii) When $n \ge 3$, for each $i = 1, 2, \dots, n-2$, the sign of $a_i - a_{i+1}$ is the opposite of the sign of $a_{i+1} - a_{i+2}$. Compute (1) $f(10)$, (2) $f(2008) \mod 13$.

paraphrase.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and $f(n)$ denote the number of $n$-digit integers $\overline{a_1a_2\cdots a_n}$ satisfying: (i) Each digit $a_i$ is from the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and $a_i \neq a_{i+1}$ for $i = 1, 2, \dots$; (ii) For $n \ge 3$, the sequence alternates between increasing and decreasing, i.e., $a_i < a_{i+1} > a_{i+2}$ or $a_i > a_{i+1} < a_{i+2}$ for all $i = 1, 2, \dots$. Determine (1) $f(10)$, (2) $f(2008) \mod 13$.

style.text:
Let $g(n)$ count the number of length-$n$ sequences $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$ such that:
(i) Each $x_i$ is from the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, and adjacent elements are distinct;
(ii) For $n \ge 3$, the sequence alternates between rising and falling: that is, for each $i$, $(x_i - x_{i+1})(x_{i+1} - x_{i+2}) < 0$.
Find (1) $g(10)$, and (2) the value of $g(2008) \mod 13$.

exact.text: Is it possible to partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 96\}$ into $32$ disjoint 3-element subsets such that all subsets have the same sum? Is it possible to partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 99\}$ into $33$ disjoint 3-element subsets such that all subsets have the same sum?

paraphrase.text: Is it possible to partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 96\}$ into $32$ groups of three numbers such that the sum of the numbers in each group is the same? Is it possible to partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 99\}$ into $33$ groups of three numbers such that the sum of the numbers in each group is the same?

style.text: Can one partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 99\}$ into $33$ triplets such that the sum of the numbers in each triplet is the same?

exact.text: Each positive integer is assigned a color: blue or red. Show that there exists an infinite sequence of positive integers $\{b_n\}$ with $b_1 < b_2 < \dots$ such that the sequence $b_1$, $\frac{b_1+b_2}{2}$, $b_2$, $\frac{b_2+b_3}{2}$, $b_3$, $\dots$ is monochromatic.

paraphrase.text: Given that each positive integer is colored either blue or red, show that there exists an infinite increasing sequence of positive integers $\{a_n\}$ such that the sequence $a_1$, $\frac{a_1+a_2}{2}$, $a_2$, $\frac{a_2+a_3}{2}$, $a_3$, $\dots$ consists entirely of elements of one color.

style.text: Given a coloring of the positive integers using only two colors, red and blue, show that there exists an increasing sequence $\{a_n\}$ of positive integers such that the sequence $a_1, \frac{a_1+a_2}{2}, a_2, \frac{a_2+a_3}{2}, a_3, \dots$ is entirely positive integers and all elements share the same color.

exact.text: Let $b_n = n\sqrt{5} - \lfloor n\sqrt{5} \rfloor$ for $n = 1, 2, \dots, 2009$. Determine the smallest and largest possible values among the set $\{b_n\}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $ f(n) = n\sqrt{5} - \lfloor n\sqrt{5} \rfloor $ for all positive integers $ n $. Determine the maximum and minimum among $ f(1), f(2), \dots, f(2009) $.

style.text: Let $ b_k = k\sqrt{5} - \left\lfloor k\sqrt{5} \right\rfloor $ for all positive integers $ k $. Determine the largest and smallest values among $ b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{2009} $.

exact.text: Given $f(x) = 3a^x + a^{2x} - 2$ with $a > 0, a \neq 1$, it attains a maximum of $8$ on $[-1, 1]$. Determine its minimum value on the same interval.

paraphrase.text: Given $g(x) = b^{2x} + 3b^x - 2$ where $b > 0$ and $b \neq 1$, it attains the maximum value $8$ on $[-1, 1]$. Determine its minimum value on the same interval.

style.text: Let $ g(x) = b^{2x} + 3b^x - 2 $ with $ b > 0, b \neq 1 $. If the maximum of $ g(x) $ on $ [-1, 1] $ is $ 8 $, find the minimum value of $ g(x) $ on the same interval.

exact.text: Given the set $M = \{1, 2, 3, ..., 50\}$, determine all positive integers $n$ for which in every 35-element subset of $M$, there exist at least two distinct elements $x$ and $y$ such that either $x + y = n$ or $|x - y| = n$.

paraphrase.text: Let set $M = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 50\}$. Determine all positive integers $n$ such that for every 35-element subset of $M$, there exist distinct elements $x$ and $y$ in the subset satisfying $x + y = n$ or $|x - y| = n$.

style.text: Given the set $S = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 50\}$, determine all positive integers $k$ such that in every 35-element subset of $S$, there exist distinct elements $x$ and $y$ satisfying $x + y = k$ or $|x - y| = k$.

exact.text: Let $O$ and $H$ be the circumcenter and orthocenter of an acute triangle $ABC$ ($A$, $H$, $O$ are not collinear). Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$, and let $E$ be the intersection of the perpendicular bisector of $AO$ with $BC$. Show that the midpoint of segment $OH$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$.

paraphrase.text: Let $O$ and $H$ be the circumcenter and orthocenter of an acute triangle $ABC$ with $A$, $O$, $H$ not collinear. Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$, and let $E$ be the intersection of the line $BC$ with the perpendicular bisector of $AO$. Show that the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ passes through the midpoint of $OH$.

style.text: In an acute triangle $ PQR $, let $ H $ be the orthocenter and $ O $ be the circumcenter ($ P $, $ H $, $ O $ are not collinear). Let $ S $ be the foot of the perpendicular from $ P $ to $ QR $, and let $ T $ be the point where the perpendicular bisector of $ PO $ intersects $ QR $. Prove that the midpoint of $ OH $ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ PST $.

exact.text: Let $H_n = 1 + \frac{1}{2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. Show that for any real numbers $a, b$ with $0 \le a < b \le 1$, the set $\{\{H_n\} : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ intersects the open interval $(a, b)$ infinitely often. (Here $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$.)

paraphrase.text: Let $H_n = 1 + \frac{1}{2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. Show that for all real numbers $a, b$ with $0 < a < b < 1$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that the fractional part of $H_n$ lies in the interval $(a, b)$.

style.text: Define $ H_n = 1 + \frac{1}{2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n} $. Show that for any real interval $ (\alpha, \beta) $ with $ 0 \le \alpha < \beta \le 1 $, the sequence $ \{H_n - \lfloor H_n \rfloor\} $ has infinitely many elements inside $ (\alpha, \beta) $.

exact.text: Let $u, v$ be positive integers. Define $\{a_n\}$ by $a_1 = u + v$, and for all $m \ge 1$, $$ a_{2m} = a_m + u, \quad a_{2m+1} = a_m + v. $$ Let $S_m = \sum_{k=1}^m a_k$. Prove that infinitely many $S_n$ are perfect squares.

paraphrase.text: Let $p, q$ be positive integers. Define the sequence $\{b_n\}$ recursively by $b_1 = p + q$, and for $m \ge 1$, $$\begin{cases} b_{2m} = b_m + p, \\ b_{2m+1} = b_m + q. \end{cases}$$ Let $T_m = b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_m$ ($m = 1, 2, \dots$). Show that infinitely many $T_n$ are perfect squares.

style.text: Let $x, y$ be positive integers, and define a sequence $\{b_n\}$ by $b_1 = x + y$, and for $n \ge 1$, $$\begin{cases} b_{2n} = b_n + x, \\ b_{2n+1} = b_n + y. \end{cases}$$ Let $T_k = b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_k$. Show that infinitely many $T_k$ are perfect squares.

exact.text: Define the set $A = \{1 + i, 1 + 2i, 1 + 3i, 2 + i, 2 + 2i, 2 + 3i, 3 + i, 3 + 2i, 3 + 3i\}$, where $i^2 = -1$. Let $\alpha = (z_1, z_2, \dots, z_9)$ be a permutation of $A$ such that $|z_1| \le |z_2| \le \dots \le |z_9|$. Determine how many such permutations $\alpha$ exist.

paraphrase.text: Let $S = \{a + bi \mid a, b \in \{1, 2, 3\}\}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit. Consider all 9-element permutations $\sigma = (w_1, w_2, \dots, w_9)$ of the elements in $S$ such that $|w_1| \le |w_2| \le \dots \le |w_9|$. How many such permutations $\sigma$ exist?

style.text: Let $S = \{a + bi \mid a, b \in \{1, 2, 3\}\}$, a 9-element set of complex numbers. Arrange all elements of $S$ in a sequence $\beta = (w_1, w_2, \dots, w_9)$ such that $|w_1| \le |w_2| \le \dots \le |w_9|$. How many such sequences $\beta$ are there?

exact.text: Let $a, b > 0$. If the equation $\sqrt{\sqrt{x^2}} + \sqrt{\sqrt{(x+a)^2}} = b$ has precisely three distinct real solutions $x_1 < x_2 < x_3 = b$, find the value of $a+b$.

paraphrase.text: Let $a, b > 0$. The equation $\sqrt{|x|} + \sqrt{|x + a|} = b$ has three distinct real roots $x_1 < x_2 < x_3 = b$. Determine the value of $a + b$.

exact.text: Let $\Gamma$ be an ellipse with major axis endpoint $P$, minor axis endpoint $Q$, and foci $G_1$, $G_2$. If $\vec{PG_1} \cdot \vec{PG_2} + \vec{QG_1} \cdot \vec{QG_2} = 0$, determine $\tan \angle PQG_1 \cdot \tan \angle PQG_2$.

paraphrase.text: Let $\Gamma$ be an ellipse with major axis endpoints $A$ and $-A$, minor axis endpoints $B$ and $-B$, and foci $F_1$ and $F_2$. If $\overrightarrow{AF_1} \cdot \overrightarrow{AF_2} + \overrightarrow{BF_1} \cdot \overrightarrow{BF_2} = 0$, determine the product $\tan \angle ABF_1 \cdot \tan \angle ABF_2$.

style.text: Let $\Gamma$ be an ellipse with major axis endpoints $P$ and $Q$, and minor axis endpoints $R$ and $S$. Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be the foci of $\Gamma$. If $\overrightarrow{PG_1} \cdot \overrightarrow{PG_2} + \overrightarrow{RG_1} \cdot \overrightarrow{RG_2} = 0$, compute $\tan \angle PRG_1 \cdot \tan \angle PRG_2$.

exact.text:
Determine the maximum $ C > 0 $ such that for each integer $ n \ge 2 $, there exist $ x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n \in [-1, 1] $ with
$$
\left( \prod_{1 \le i < j \le n} (x_i - x_j) \right)^{\frac{2}{n(n-1)}} \ge C.
$$

paraphrase.text:
Determine the maximum value of $ C > 0 $, such that for all integers $ n \ge 2 $, there exist real numbers $ a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \in [-1, 1] $ with
$$
\prod_{\substack{i,j = 1 \\ i < j}}^{n} (a_i - a_j) \ge C^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

style.text:
Determine the maximum value of $ C > 0 $, such that for each integer $ n \ge 2 $, there exist $ n $ real numbers $ a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n $ in the interval $ [-1, 1] $ for which
$$
\prod_{1 \le i < j \le n} (a_i - a_j) \ge C^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}.
$$

exact.text: The maximum of $ f(x) = 2 \sin^2 x - \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} $ is ______.

paraphrase.text: Find the maximum value of the function $g(x) = 2 \sin^2 x - \sec^2 x + 1$.

style.text: Find the maximum value of $g(\theta) = 2 \cos^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta$.

exact.text: Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers, and $p_1, p_2, \dots, p_r$ be distinct primes. A blackboard initially contains all products $\prod_{j=1}^r p_j^{i_j}$ with $0 \le i_j \le n$. Alice and Bob alternate turns (Alice starts) by replacing two numbers with either their gcd or lcm (Alice uses gcd, Bob uses lcm). Determine the smallest $M$ such that Alice can ensure the final number is $\le M$.

paraphrase.text: Let $r$ be a positive integer and $p_1, p_2, \dots, p_r$ be distinct primes. Suppose $n$ is a positive integer and the blackboard initially contains all products $\prod_{j=1}^r p_j^{e_j}$ with $0 \le e_j \le n$. Alice and Bob alternately perform operations on the blackboard: Alice replaces two numbers with their greatest common divisor, and Bob replaces two numbers with their least common multiple. Alice moves first. Determine the smallest integer $M$ such that Alice can ensure the final number on the blackboard is at most $M$.

style.text: Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers, and $q_1$, $q_2$, $\dots$, $q_r$ be distinct prime numbers. A board initially contains all products $q_1^{a_1} q_2^{a_2} \cdots q_r^{a_r}$ where each $a_i$ satisfies $0 \le a_i \le n$. Players alternate turns: Alice removes two numbers and writes their GCD, while Bob removes two numbers and writes their LCM. The game ends when only one number remains. Determine the smallest $M$ such that Alice can ensure the final number is at most $M$.

exact.text: Let $m$ be a real number and define $z_1 = 1 + 2i$, $z_2 = m + 3i$, where $i^2 = -1$. If the product $z_1 \cdot \bar{z_2}$ has no real part, compute the modulus of $z_1 + z_2$.

paraphrase.text: Let $a$ be a real number, and define complex numbers $w_1 = 1 + 2i$ and $w_2 = a + 3i$, with $i$ being the imaginary unit. If $w_1 \cdot \bar{w_2}$ has no real part, find the modulus of $w_1 + w_2$.

style.text: Let $m$ be a real number, and define $w_1 = 1 + 2i$, $w_2 = m + 3i$. If $w_1 \cdot \overline{w_2}$ is purely imaginary, compute $|w_1 + w_2|$.

exact.text: Determine the range of $ y = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin 2x $ for $ x $ in the interval $ \left[\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] $.

paraphrase.text: Determine the range of $ y = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin 2x $ for $ \frac{\pi}{4} \le x \le \frac{\pi}{2} $.

style.text: Find the range of $ y = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin 2x $ for $ \frac{\pi}{4} \le x \le \frac{\pi}{2} $.

exact.text: In a rectangular coordinate system $xOy$, consider the graph of $y = \frac{1}{|x|}$ denoted by $\Gamma$. Let points $P$ and $Q$ lie on $\Gamma$ such that $P$ is in the first quadrant, $Q$ is in the second quadrant, and the line $PQ$ is tangent to $\Gamma$ at $Q$. Determine the minimum value of the distance $|PQ|$.

paraphrase.text: Consider the curve $\Gamma$ given by $y = \frac{1}{|x|}$ in the $xOy$ coordinate system. Let $P$ lie in the first quadrant and $Q$ lie in the second quadrant on $\Gamma$, such that the line segment $PQ$ is tangent to the second-quadrant portion of $\Gamma$ at $Q$. Determine the smallest possible length of $PQ$.

style.text: Consider the curve $\Gamma$ defined by $y = \frac{1}{|x|}$ in the coordinate plane. Let $A$ be a point in the first quadrant and $B$ be a point in the second quadrant, both lying on $\Gamma$, such that the line $AB$ is tangent to $\Gamma$ at $B$. Find the minimum possible length of segment $AB$.

exact.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2n+1}$ be $2n+1$ positive real numbers. For $j = 1, 2, \dots, 2n+1$, define
$$
\displaystyle c_j = \max_{0 \le t \le n} \left( \frac{1}{2t+1} \sum_{\ell = j - t}^{j + t} x_\ell \right),
$$\nwhere indices are taken modulo $2n+1$. Prove: the number of indices $j$ such that $c_j \ge 1$ is at most $2 \sum_{\ell=1}^{2n+1} x_\ell$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2n+1}$ be $2n+1$ positive real numbers. For $k = 1, 2, \dots, 2n+1$, define
$$\nc_k = \max_{0 \le r \le n} \left( \frac{1}{2r+1} \sum_{j=k-r}^{k+r} x_j \right),
$$\nwhere the index of $x_j$ is considered modulo $2n+1$. Prove: the number of indices $k$ such that $c_k \ge 1$ is at most $2 \sum_{j=1}^{2n+1} x_j$.

style.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2n+1}$ be $2n+1$ positive real numbers. For $j = 1, 2, \dots, 2n+1$, define
$$
 y_j = \max_{0 \le r \le n} \left( \frac{1}{2r+1} \sum_{\ell=j-r}^{j+r} x_\ell \right),
$$\nwith indices taken modulo $2n+1$. Prove: the number of indices $j$ for which $y_j \ge 1$ is at most $2 \sum_{\ell=1}^{2n+1} x_\ell$.

exact.text: Let $g(x)$ be a function such that for all $x \neq 0$, $$ g(x) = g(1) \cdot x + \frac{g(2)}{x} - 1. $$ Find the minimum value of $g(x)$ for $x > 0$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $g(x)$ be a function defined for all $x \ne 0$ such that
$$
 g(x) = a x + \frac{b}{x} - 1,
$$\nwhere $a = g(1)$ and $b = g(2)$. Determine the minimum value of $g(x)$ on $(0, +\infty)$.

style.text: Let $ g(x) $ be a function defined for all $ x \neq 0 $ such that $$ g(x) = g(\sqrt{2}) \cdot x + \frac{g(\sqrt{3})}{x} - 1. $$ Determine the minimum of $ g(x) $ over $ (0, +\infty) $.

exact.text: In a coordinate system $xOy$, consider the parabola $\Gamma: y^2 = 2px$ with $p > 0$. A line passing through point $P(3, 2)$ with slope $1$ intersects $\Gamma$ at another point $Q$. Determine the area of triangle $\triangle OPQ$.

paraphrase.text: In a coordinate plane $xOy$, the parabola $\Gamma$ is defined by $y^2 = 2px$ for $p > 0$. A line with slope $1$ intersects $\Gamma$ at $P(3, 2)$ and another point $Q$. Find the area of triangle $\triangle OPQ$.

style.text: In the coordinate plane $xOy$, the parabola $\Gamma: y^2 = 2px$ ($p > 0$) is intersected by a line with slope $1$ at point $A(3, 2)$ and another point $B$. Determine the area of triangle $OAB$.

exact.text: Suppose real numbers $\gamma, \delta$ are such that $\lfloor n_1\gamma \rfloor \neq \lfloor n_2\delta \rfloor$ for all $n_1, n_2 \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. Show that there exist positive integers $p, q$ with $\frac{p}{\gamma} + \frac{q}{\delta} = 1$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose real numbers $\alpha, \beta$ are such that $\lfloor k_1\alpha \rfloor$ is distinct from $\lfloor k_2\beta \rfloor$ for all $k_1, k_2 \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. Prove that there are positive integers $m_1, m_2$ for which $\frac{m_1}{\alpha} + \frac{m_2}{\beta} = 1$.

style.text: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers such that for every pair of positive integers $p$ and $q$, $\lfloor pa \rfloor \neq \lfloor qb \rfloor$. Show that there exist positive integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$.

exact.text:
Let $k$, $m$, and $e$ be integers such that $e \ge 0$, $|k| \ge 2$, and $m \ge (|k| + 1)^{e+1}$. Suppose $g(x)$ is a real-coefficient polynomial of degree $e$, and for each positive integer $n$, define $s_n$ as the remainder of $\lfloor g(n)k^n \rfloor$ modulo $m$.

*Proof:* If the sequence $s_n$ is ultimately periodic, then $g(x)$ is a rational-coefficient polynomial.

paraphrase.text:
Let $c$, $k$, and $e$ be integers with $e \ge 0$, $|c| \ge 2$, and $k \ge (|c| + 1)^{e+1}$. Suppose $g(x)$ is a real-coefficient polynomial of degree $e$, and for each positive integer $m$, define $s_m$ as the remainder of $\lfloor g(m)c^m \rfloor$ modulo $k$.

*Proof:* If the sequence $s_m$ is ultimately periodic, then $g(x)$ is a rational-coefficient polynomial.

style.text:
Let $c$, $m$, and $k$ be integers with $k \ge 0$, $|c| \ge 2$, and $m \ge (|c| + 1)^{k+1}$. Suppose $g(x)$ is a real-coefficient polynomial of degree $k$, and for each positive integer $n$, define $s_n$ as the remainder of $\lfloor g(n)c^n \rfloor$ modulo $m$.

*Proof:* If the sequence $s_n$ is ultimately periodic, then $g(x)$ is a rational-coefficient polynomial.

exact.text:
Let $\{b_n\}$ be a sequence defined recursively by $b_1 = 0$, and for all $n \ge 2$,
$$\nb_n = \frac{1}{n} + \frac{1}{\left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil} \sum_{k=1}^{\left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil} b_k.
$$
Determine the largest value in the sequence $\{b_n\}$.

paraphrase.text:
Define a sequence $\{b_n\}$ by $b_1 = 0$, and for $n \ge 2$,
$$\nb_n = \frac{1}{n} + \frac{1}{m_n} \sum_{k=1}^{m_n} b_k,
$$\nwhere $m_n = \left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil$. Determine the maximum value among all $b_n$.

style.text:
Let $\{b_n\}$ be a sequence such that $b_1 = 0$, and for each integer $n \ge 2$,
$$\nb_n = \frac{1}{n} + \frac{1}{\left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil} \sum_{j=1}^{\left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil} b_j.
$$
Determine the largest value in the sequence $\{b_n\}$.

Let $q_1, q_2, \dots, q_{2025}$ be real numbers, and let $\{b_n^{(1)}\}_{n \ge 0}$, $\{b_n^{(2)}\}_{n \ge 0}$, $\dots$, $\{b_n^{(2025)}\}_{n \ge 0}$ be $2025$ real sequences satisfying:
(1) $b_0^{(i)}$ ($1 \le i \le 2025$) are all zero;
(2) $b_1^{(i)}$ ($1 \le i \le 2025$) are **not** all zero;
(3) For $i = 1, 2, \dots, 2025$ and any positive integer $n$,
$$
 b_{n-1}^{(i)} + b_n^{(i)} + b_{n+1}^{(i)} = q_i \cdot b_n^{(i+1)},
$$\nwhere $b_n^{(2026)} = b_n^{(1)}$.
Prove that there exists a positive real number $r$ and infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that
$$
 \max \{ |b_n^{(1)}|, |b_n^{(2)}|, \dots, |b_n^{(2025)}| \} > r.
$$

exact.text:
Determine all integer-valued functions $f$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ such that:
(1) For each positive integer $M$, there is an integer $k$ with $f(k)^2 \ge M^2$;
(2) For all integers $m, n$,
$$2f(m)f(n) - f(m - n) - 1$$ is the square of an integer.

paraphrase.text: Find all functions $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ such that: (1) For any positive integer $M$, there exists an integer $k$ with $f(k)^2 \ge M^2$; (2) For all integers $a, b$, $$2f(a)f(b) - f(a - b) - 1$$ is a square of an integer.

style.text:
Determine all integer-valued functions $ g : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z} $ such that:
(i) For every $ N \in \mathbb{Z}^+ $, there is some $ x \in \mathbb{Z} $ with $ |g(x)| \ge N $;
(ii) For all integers $ a, b $, the expression
$$ 2g(a)g(b) - g(a - b) - 1 $$\nis a square number.

exact.text:
Given any real number $q \ge 1$, consider the set of real numbers $x$ satisfying
$$\nq < x < \left(\sqrt{q + \frac{1}{4}} + 2\right)^2
$$
Prove that there exist four distinct natural numbers $a, b, c, d$ in the set such that $ab = cd$.

paraphrase.text: Let $p$ be any real number satisfying $p \ge 1$. Consider the interval $$ (p, \left(2 + \sqrt{p + \frac{1}{4}}\right)^2) $$ of real numbers. Prove that it is possible to find four distinct natural numbers $a, b, c, d$ in this interval such that $ab = cd$.

style.text: Given a real number $ r \ge 1 $, define the set of real numbers $ y $ such that $$ r < y < \left(2 + \sqrt{r + \frac{1}{4}}\right)^2 $$ Prove that there exist four distinct natural numbers $ w, x, y, z $ in this interval with $ wz = xy $.

exact.text: Determine all positive integer triples $(k, m, n)$ such that a square of side length $m$ can be tiled with a number of $1 \times k$ rectangles and a single square of side length $n$.

paraphrase.text: Determine all positive integer triples $(a, b, c)$ such that a square of side length $b$ can be tiled with several $1 \times a$ rectangles and a single square of side length $c$.

style.text: Determine all positive integers $(a, b, c)$ such that a square of side $b$ can be tiled using several $1 \times a$ rectangles and a single square of side $c$.

exact.text: \text{Let } \mathbb{R}^+ \text{ be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions } f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+ \text{ satisfying} \$$ (1 - y f(x + y))(1 + y f(x)) = 1 \$$ for any $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$.

paraphrase.text:
Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ satisfying
$$
(1 + a f(b))(1 - a f(b + a)) = 1
$$\nfor any $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+$.

style.text: \text{Let } \mathbb{R}^+ \text{ be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions } g: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+ \text{ satisfying} \$$ (1 + a g(b))(1 - a g(b + a)) = 1 \$$ \text{for all } a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+.

exact.text:
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $M$ and $N$ as the midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. Points $K$ and $L$ lie on $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, such that $\angle KAM = \angle LCN$. If the lines $BD$, $KM$, and $LN$ are concurrent, prove that
$$
\angle KMN = \angle BDC, \quad \angle LNM = \angle ABD
$$

paraphrase.text: In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, suppose $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. Points $K$ and $L$ lie on $AB$ and $CD$ respectively, such that $\angle AKM = \angle CLN$. If the lines $BD$, $KM$, and $LN$ are concurrent, show that $$\angle KMN = \angle BDC, \quad \angle LNM = \angle ABD$$

style.text:
In a convex quadrilateral $PQRS$, let $U$ and $V$ be midpoints of sides $PS$ and $QR$, respectively. Points $X$ and $Y$ are chosen on sides $PQ$ and $RS$, respectively, such that $\angle UX P = \angle V Y R$. Prove that if lines $QS$, $XU$, and $YV$ are concurrent, then
$$
\angle XUV = \angle QRS, \quad \angle YVU = \angle QSP.
$$

exact.text: Suppose $P(x)$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients such that for any integer-coefficient polynomials $F(x)$, $G(x)$, and $Q(x)$, the identity $$P(Q(x)) = F(x) \cdot G(x)$$ implies that at least one of $F(x)$ or $G(x)$ is a constant. Prove that $P(x)$ must be a constant polynomial.

paraphrase.text: Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Suppose that for any integer-coefficient polynomials $A(x)$, $B(x)$, and $R(x)$, the equation $$P(R(x)) = A(x) \cdot B(x)$$ implies that either $A(x)$ or $B(x)$ is constant. Prove that $P(x)$ must be a constant polynomial.

style.text: Let $R(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that for all polynomials $A(x)$, $B(x)$, $S(x)$ with integer coefficients, if $$R(S(x)) = A(x) \cdot B(x)$$ then at least one of $A(x)$ or $B(x)$ is a constant polynomial. Show that $R(x)$ must be a constant polynomial.

exact.text:
Prove that for any real $x > 0$ and integer $n > 0$,
$$
\left(x^n + x^{-n} - 2\right) \ge n^2 \left(x + x^{-1} - 2\right).
$$

paraphrase.text:
Prove that for all positive real numbers $a$ and positive integers $k$, the inequality
$$
 a^k + \frac{1}{a^k} - 2 \ge k^2 \left(a + \frac{1}{a} - 2\right)
$$\nholds.

style.text:
Prove that for all positive real numbers $a$ and positive integers $k$, the inequality
$$
 a^k + \frac{1}{a^k} - 2 \ge k^2 \left(a + \frac{1}{a} - 2\right)
$$\nholds.

exact.text: For a positive integer $n$, let $\langle A_{i,j} \rangle_{1\le i,j\le n}$ be a family of sets. The configuration is called *sweet* if for all $1 \le i \le n-1$ and all $j$ such that $1 \le j \le n$, both $A_{i,j} \subseteq A_{i+1,j}$ and $A_{j,i} \subseteq A_{j,i+1}$ hold. Define $f(n,k)$ as the number of such configurations with $A_{n,n} \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$. Which is greater: $f(2024, 2024^2)$ or $f(2024^2, 2024)$?

paraphrase.text: Let $ n $ be a positive integer. An $ n $-array is a collection $ \langle B_{p,q} \rangle_{1\le p,q\le n} $ of sets. We say an $ n $-array is *sweet* if for all $ 1 \le p \le n-1 $, $ 1 \le q \le n $, both $ B_{p,q} \subseteq B_{p+1,q} $ and $ B_{q,p} \subseteq B_{q,p+1} $ hold. Define $ g(n,k) $ as the number of sweet $ n $-arrays where $ B_{n,n} \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, k\} $. Which is greater: $ g(2024, 2024^2) $ or $ g(2024^2, 2024) $?

style.text: For a positive integer $m$, an $m$-grid is a collection of sets $\langle B_{p,q} \rangle_{1\le p,q\le m}$. An $m$-grid is called *nice* if for all $1 \le p < m$ and $1 \le q \le m$, $B_{p,q} \subseteq B_{p+1,q}$ and $B_{q,p} \subseteq B_{q,p+1}$. Define $g(m,r)$ as the number of nice $m$-grids such that $B_{m,m} \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$. Which is larger: $g(2024, 2024^2)$ or $g(2024^2, 2024)$?

exact.text: Let $\{b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers defined by the recurrence $$ b_{n+1} = (n + 1)(b_n - n + 1), $$ for all $n \ge 1$. Find the largest positive integer $k$ such that $\gcd(b_i, b_{i+1}) = k$ for some $i \ge 2$, expressed in terms of $b_1$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $\{b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is a sequence of positive integers defined by the recurrence $b_{n+1} = (n + 1)(b_n - n + 1)$ for all $n \ge 1$. If $b_1 = a_1$, find the largest integer $k$ such that $\gcd(b_i, b_{i+1}) = k$ for some $i \ge 2$.

style.text:
Consider a sequence $\{b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers defined by the recurrence
$$\nb_{n+1} = (n + 1)(b_n - n + 1)
$$\nfor all $n \ge 1$. For some $j \ge 2$, find the largest integer $k$ such that $\gcd(b_j, b_{j+1}) = k$, in terms of $b_1$.

exact.text: Given that positive real numbers $x, y, z$ satisfy $5xyz > x^3 + y^3 + z^3$, prove that $x, y, z$ can be the sides of a triangle.

paraphrase.text: Show that for positive real numbers $x, y, z$, the condition $5xyz > x^3 + y^3 + z^3$ implies that $x, y, z$ can be the lengths of the sides of a triangle.

style.text: Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers such that $5xyz > x^3 + y^3 + z^3$. Show that $x, y, z$ can be the side lengths of a triangle.

exact.text:
Given a set of 21 distinct integers, for any partition into two subsets of 11 and 10 elements, the sum of the subset with 11 elements is strictly greater than the sum of the subset with 10 elements.
\na) Prove that all elements are strictly greater than 100.
\nb) Determine all such sets of 21 distinct integers that include the number 101.

paraphrase.text: \text{Given 21 distinct integers, the sum of any 11 of them is strictly greater than the sum of the other 10.}\\\text{a) Prove that each integer in the group is greater than 100.}\\\text{b) Determine all such sets of 21 distinct integers that include 101 as an element.}

style.text:
Let $ S $ be a set of 21 distinct integers such that the total of any 11 elements is strictly larger than the total of the remaining 10.
\na) Show that all elements of $ S $ are greater than 100.
\nb) Determine all such sets $ S $ that include the number 101.

exact.text:
Let $p(n)$ count the number of length-$n$ sequences of digits from $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ where no two consecutive digits are within 1 of each other. Prove that for all positive integers $n$,
$$
5 \cdot 2.4^{n-1} \le p(n) \le 5 \cdot 2.5^{n-1}.
$$

paraphrase.text:
Let $q(n)$ count the number of sequences of length $n$ where each term is an integer from $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ and the difference between any two consecutive terms is at least $2$. Prove that for every positive integer $n$,
$$
5 \cdot 2.4^{n-1} \le q(n) \le 5 \cdot 2.5^{n-1}.
$$

style.text:
Let $a_n$ count the number of $n$-length strings using only the characters $A, B, C, D, E$ such that any two consecutive characters are not adjacent in the alphabet. Show that for all $n \ge 1$,
$$
5 \cdot 2.4^{n-1} \le a_n \le 5 \cdot 2.5^{n-1}.
$$

exact.text: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. There are four rooms with some objects in each. In each step, we transfer $\frac{1}{n}$ of the objects in a room to the next one in a cyclic order (1→2→3→4→1). All object counts remain integers throughout. After the full cycle, all rooms contain the same number of objects. Determine the minimal number of objects in the second room at the end and for which value of $n$ this minimum is achieved.

paraphrase.text: Four rooms each contain some number of objects. Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. One $n$-th of the objects from the first room is transferred to the second, then one $n$-th of the (updated) number of objects in the second room is moved to the third, and so on cyclically through the rooms. All movements involve only whole units of objects. After all four transfers, each room has the same number of objects. What is the smallest number of objects that can end up in the second room? For which values of $n$ does this minimum occur?

style.text: There are tokens in four boxes. Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. We transfer $\frac{1}{n}$ of the tokens in the first box to the second one. Then $\frac{1}{n}$ of the tokens in the second box (after the transfer) are moved to the third box. Then the same process continues from the third to the fourth, and finally from the fourth to the first. All transfers must be in whole tokens. In the end, all boxes have equal numbers of tokens. What is the smallest possible number of tokens in the second box at the end? For which values of $n$ does this minimum occur?

exact.text: Find all integer pairs $(p, q)$ with $p = kq$ for some integer $k$ such that the equation $x^2 + px + q = 0$ has an integer solution.

paraphrase.text: Find all integer pairs $(a, b)$ with $a$ divisible by $b$ such that the equation $x^2 + ax + b = 0$ has an integer solution.

style.text: Find all integer pairs $(a, b)$ such that $a$ is a multiple of $b$ and the equation $x^2 + ax + b = 0$ has an integer solution.

exact.text: Suppose $n$ points are placed in the plane such that no three are collinear, with $n \ge 3$. Let $\phi$ be the smallest interior angle found among all triangles formed by these points. Determine the maximum possible value of $\phi$ for a fixed $n$.

paraphrase.text: Let there be $n$ points in the plane, with $n \ge 3$ and no three collinear. Among all angles formed as interior angles of triangles with vertices among these points, let $\phi$ be the smallest such angle. Determine the maximum possible value of $\phi$ for a given $n$.

style.text: Suppose $ n $ distinct points are placed in the plane, $ n \ge 3 $, such that no three are on a line. Among all triangles formed by these points, let $ \phi $ be the smallest interior angle. What is the maximum possible value of $ \phi $, as a function of $ n $?

exact.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with altitudes from $A$, $B$, and $C$ meeting $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $K$, $L$, and $M$, respectively. Prove that $ABC$ is isosceles if and only if $$ AM + BK + CL = AL + BM + CK. $$

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with altitudes $AK$, $BL$, $CM$. Show that triangle $ABC$ is isosceles if and only if $$ AL + BM + CK = AM + BK + CL. $$

style.text: Let triangle $PQR$ be acute, with altitudes from $P$, $Q$, and $R$ meeting the opposite sides at points $X$, $Y$, and $Z$, respectively. Prove that triangle $PQR$ is isosceles if and only if $$ PX + QY + RZ = QX + RY + PZ. $$

exact.text:
Find all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ such that for all real numbers $ a, b $, the identity
$$\nf(b - ab) = f(a)b + (a - 1)^2 f(b)
$$\nholds.

paraphrase.text: Determine all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ satisfying the identity $$ f(y(1 - x)) = f(x)y + (x - 1)^2 f(y) $$ for all real numbers $ x, y $.

style.text: Determine all functions $ g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} $ such that for all real numbers $ a, b $, $$ g(b - ab) = g(a)b + (a - 1)^2 g(b). $$

exact.text:
Let $k \neq 0$ be an integer. Prove that the number of integer solutions $(x, y)$ with $x + y \neq 0$ to the equation
$$
(x + y)k = x^2 - xy + 2y^2
$$\nis finite.

paraphrase.text:
Let $m 
eq 0$ be an integer. Prove that the number of integer solutions $(a, b)$ to the equation
$$
m =  rac{a^2 - ab + 2b^2}{a + b}
$$
remains finite.

style.text: \text{Let } a \neq 0 \text{ be an integer. Prove that the number of integer solutions } (m, n) \text{ to the equation } a = \frac{m^2 - mn + 2n^2}{m + n} \text{ is finite and depends on } a.

exact.text: Determine all integer solutions $(a, b, c)$ for which each of the expressions $$\frac{a}{b + c}, \quad \frac{b}{c + a}, \quad \frac{c}{a + b}$$ evaluates to an integer.

paraphrase.text: Determine all integer solutions $(x, y, z)$ such that $$\frac{x}{y+z}, \quad \frac{y}{z+x}, \quad \frac{z}{x+y}$$ are all integers.

style.text: Determine all integer solutions $(x, y, z)$ such that $$\frac{x}{y+z}, \quad \frac{y}{z+x}, \quad \frac{z}{x+y}$$ are all integers.

exact.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with incenter $I$. Let the rays $BI$ and $CI$ intersect the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ again at $S$ and $T$, respectively. If the line $ST$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $K$ and $L$, prove that quadrilateral $AKIL$ is a rhombus.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with incenter $I$. Let the ray $BI$ intersect the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ again at $S$ (distinct from $B$), and let the ray $CI$ intersect it again at $T$ (distinct from $C$). Suppose the segment $ST$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively. Prove that quadrilateral $AKIL$ is a rhombus.

style.text: Let triangle $PQR$ be acute, with incenter $J$. Extend $QJ$ and $RJ$ to meet the circumcircle of triangle $PQR$ again at $M \neq Q$, $N \neq R$, respectively. Let $MN$ intersect $PQ$ and $PR$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that $PXYJ$ is a rhombus.

exact.text: Let $G$ be a graph with $50$ vertices and $225$ edges. A triple of distinct vertices is called *connected* if the induced subgraph on these three vertices contains at least two edges. Find the minimum and maximum number of such connected triples that can exist in $G$.

paraphrase.text: Let $G$ be a graph with $n = 50$ vertices and $m = 225$ edges. A triple of distinct vertices is called *connected* if at least two of the three possible edges among them are present in $G$. Find the minimum and maximum number of such connected triples in $G$.

style.text: Suppose a simple graph has $50$ nodes and $225$ links. A set of three distinct nodes is called \textit{linked} if the set contains at least two connections. Find the minimum and maximum number of such linked sets.

exact.text: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a^2 + b = a + b^2$. Determine the minimum possible value of this common expression.

paraphrase.text: Let $x, y$ be real numbers such that $x^2 + y = x + y^2$. Find the minimum value that this common expression can take.

style.text: Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers satisfying $x^2 + y = x + y^2$. Find the minimum possible value of $x^2 + y$.

exact.text:
Find the number of quadratic polynomials $P(x)$ with integer coefficients satisfying:
$$
 P(x) > x^2 + 2x - 2023 \quad \text{and} \quad P(x) < 2x^2
$$\nfor all real $x$.

paraphrase.text:
Find how many quadratic polynomials $Q(x)$ with integer coefficients exist such that for every real number $x$,
$$
\quad x^2 + 2x - 2023 < Q(x) < 2x^2.
$$

style.text:
Find how many quadratic polynomials $Q(x)$ with integer coefficients satisfy the inequality for all real numbers $x$:
$$
 x^2 + 2x - 2023 < Q(x) < 2x^2.
$$

exact.text: Let $n > 1$ be a positive integer with largest prime factor $p$. For every non-empty subset of the divisors of $n$, write the sum of its elements on the board. If more than $p$ distinct values from $\{1, 2, \dots, p+2\}$ are written, and no number from this set is repeated, show that no number is written more than once.

paraphrase.text: Let $n > 1$ be a positive integer with largest prime divisor $p$. For every nonempty subset of the set of divisors of $n$, write the sum of the elements of the subset on the board. If the board contains more than $p$ distinct numbers from the set $\{1, 2, \dots, p+2\}$, and all these numbers appear only once, show that all numbers on the board are unique.

style.text: Let $m > 1$ be a positive integer and $q$ its largest prime factor. Consider the set of all nonempty subsets of the divisors of $m$, and for each such subset, record the sum of its elements. If more than $q$ of the numbers in the set $\{1, 2, \dots, q+2\}$ are recorded, and each of these numbers appears only once in the process, prove that all numbers recorded are distinct.

Sei $S$ die Menge aller Paare $(a, b)$ mit nichtnegativen ganzen Zahlen $a$ und $b$. Bestimme alle Funktionen $g: S \rightarrow \mathrm{IR}$, die folgende Bedingung erfüllen:
$$\ng(a, b) = 
\left\{\begin{array}{c}
0 \quad \text{wenn } ab = 0 \\
1 + \frac{1}{2} g(a+1, b-1) + \frac{1}{2} g(a-1, b+1) \text{ sonst }
\end{array} .\right.
$$

exact.text: Man beweise, dass es keine natürliche Zahl $m$ gibt, sodass für $j=2,3, \ldots, 10$ die erste Ziffer in der Dezimaldarstellung von $(m - 1 + j)!$ gleich $j - 1$ ist.

paraphrase.text: Man beweise, dass es keine natürliche Zahl $n$ gibt, sodass für alle $k=1,2,\ldots,9$ die erste Ziffer der Dezimaldarstellung von $(n+k)!$ gleich $k$ ist.

style.text: Zeige, dass es keine natürliche Zahl $m$ gibt, sodass für alle $i = 1, 2, \ldots, 9$ die erste Dezimalziffer von $(m+i)!$ gleich $i$ ist.

exact.text: Man zeige, dass in den Dezimalstellen von $\sqrt[3]{3}$ zwischen Position $10^6$ und $\pi \cdot 10^6$ mindestens eine Ziffer nicht gleich 2 ist.

paraphrase.text: Man zeige, dass es in der Dezimalentwicklung von $\sqrt[3]{3}$ mindestens eine Ziffer außer 2 zwischen der 1000000. und 3141592. Stelle nach dem Komma gibt.

style.text: Zeige, dass es in der Dezimalentwicklung von $\sqrt[3]{3}$ mindestens eine Ziffer $\neq 2$ zwischen der 1-Millionsten und der 3141592-ten Nachkommastelle gibt.

exact.text:
Bestimme alle Paare $(m, n)$ mit $m, n \in \mathbb{N}_0$, die der Gleichung
$$
3^{m} = 7^{n} + 2
$$\nerfüllen.

paraphrase.text:
Bestimme alle Paare $(x, y)$ nicht-negativer ganzer Zahlen, die die Gleichung
$$
3^{x} - 7^{y} = 2
$$\nerfüllen.

style.text: Finde alle Paare $(a, b)$ nicht-negativer ganzer Zahlen, welche die Gleichung $$7^{b} + 2 = 3^{a}$$ erfüllen.

exact.text: Bestimme die minimale natürliche Zahl $n$, so dass jede Familie von reellen Zahlen $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{d}$ mit $\sum_{i=1}^{d} a_{i} = 2013$ und $0 \leq a_{i} \leq 1$ für alle $i$ in $n$ Teilmengen aufgeteilt werden kann, wobei jede Teilmenge eine Summe $\leq 1$ hat.

paraphrase.text: Bestimme die minimale Anzahl $n$ von Teilmengen, in die man eine Menge von reellen Zahlen $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{d}$ mit $0 \leq x_{i} \leq 1$ und $x_{1}+x_{2}+\ldots+x_{d}=2013$ immer aufteilen kann, so dass jede Teilmenge eine Summe von höchstens 1 hat.

style.text: Bestimme die kleinste natürliche Zahl $n$, so dass jede endliche Menge von reellen Zahlen $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k$ mit $0 \leq x_i \leq 1$ und $x_1 + x_2 + \ldots + x_k = 2013$ sich in $n$ disjunkte Teilmengen zerlegen lässt, bei denen die Summe der Elemente in jeder Teilmenge kleiner oder gleich 1 ist.

exact.text: Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Betrachte disjunkte Paare $(a, b)$ aus der Menge $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, wobei $a + b \leq n$ gilt. Bestimme mit Begründung die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, wobei alle Summen $a + b$ paarweise verschieden sein müssen. (Ein Beispiel für $n = 10$ wären $(1,9), (2,7), (3,5)$.)

paraphrase.text: Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Man betrachte disjunkte Paare $(a_i, b_i)$ mit $a_i, b_i \in \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, wobei alle $a_i$ und $b_i$ eindeutig sind. Bestimme die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, so dass alle Paarsummen $a_i + b_i$ paarweise verschieden und $\leq n$ sind.

style.text: Sei $n$ eine natürliche Zahl. Wir betrachten disjunkte Paare $(a_i, b_i)$ aus der Menge $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, wobei jedes Element in höchstens einem Paar vorkommt. Bestimme mit Begründung die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, bei denen alle Paarsummen $a_i + b_i$ eindeutig und kleiner oder gleich $n$ sind. (Ein Beispiel für $n=10$ wären die Paare $(1, 9), (2, 7), (3, 5)$.)

exact.text: Bestimmen Sie alle Paare $(a, b)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen, sodass es eine positive ganze Zahl $n$ gibt mit $\tau(n a) = \tau(n b)$, wobei $\tau(k)$ die Anzahl der positiven Teiler von $k$ bezeichnet.

paraphrase.text: Bestimmen Sie alle Paare $(x, y)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen, sodass es eine positive ganze Zahl $m$ gibt, für die die Anzahl der Divisoren von $m x$ und $m y$ übereinstimmt.

style.text: Bestimmen Sie alle Paare $(x, y)$ natürlicher Zahlen, für die es eine natürliche Zahl $k$ gibt, sodass $kx$ und $ky$ dieselbe Anzahl an positiven Teilern haben.

exact.text:
Gegeben sei eine positive ganze Zahl $k$, und es sei $K$ die Menge aller Gitterpunkte $(x, y)$ mit $x, y \in \{0, 1, \ldots, 2k - 1\}$. Somit gilt $|K| = 4k^{2}$.

Sei $V$ eine Menge von $k^2$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken, wobei gilt:
\ni) Alle Ecken der Vierecke in $V$ liegen in $K$.
\nii) Jeder Punkt aus $K$ ist genau an einem Viereck aus $V$ als Ecke beteiligt.

Bestimmen Sie den maximal möglichen Wert der Gesamtfläche aller Vierecke in $V$.

paraphrase.text:
Sei $k$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Sei $K$ die Menge aller Punkte $(x, y)$ mit $x, y \in \{0, 1, \dots, 2k - 1\}$. Es gilt $|K| = 4k^2$.

Sei $V$ eine Menge von $k^2$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken, bei denen

i) alle Ecken zu $K$ gehören,
ii) jeder Punkt in $K$ genau einmal als Ecke in einem Viereck aus $V$ vorkommt.

Bestimmen Sie den maximal möglichen Wert der Gesamtfläche aller Vierecke in $V$.

style.text: Sei $k$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Betrachte das Gitter $K$ aller Punkte $(x, y)$ mit $x, y \in \{0, 1, \ldots, 2k-1\}$. Sei $V$ eine Menge von $k^2$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken, wobei alle Eckpunkte in $K$ liegen und jeder Punkt in $K$ genau einem Viereck als Ecke dient. Bestimme den maximal möglichen Wert der Summe der Flächeninhalte aller Vierecke in $V$.

exact.text: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $$\frac{1}{p+1} + \frac{1}{q} = \frac{2}{n+2}$$ for some positive integer $n$. Determine all possible values of $q - p$.

paraphrase.text: \text{Let } a \text{ and } b \text{ be prime numbers such that } \frac{a}{a+1} + \frac{b+1}{b} = \frac{2m}{m+2} \text{ for some positive integer } m. \text{ Determine all values of } b - a.

style.text: \text{Two primes } a \text{ and } b \text{ satisfy } \quad \frac{a}{a+1} + \frac{b+1}{b} = \frac{2m}{m+2} \quad \text{for a positive integer } m. \text{ Determine all possible values of } b - a.

exact.text: Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_k$ be the positive integers less than $N$ that are relatively prime to $N$. Determine all $N \geq 3$ such that for every $1 \leq j < k$, $\gcd(N, a_j + a_{j+1}) > 1$.

paraphrase.text: Let $N$ be a positive integer greater than or equal to 3, and define $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_k$ to be the integers less than $N$ that are relatively prime to $N$. Determine all such $N$ for which $\gcd(N, a_i + a_{i + 1}) > 1$ holds for every $i$ with $1 \leq i \leq k - 1$.

style.text:
Let $ N $ be a positive integer $ \geq 3 $, and consider the sequence $ a_{1} < a_{2} < \dots < a_{k} $ of all numbers less than $ N $ that share no common factor with $ N $. Determine all such $ N $ for which
$$
\gcd(N, a_{j} + a_{j + 1}) > 1
$$\nfor each $ 1 \leq j \leq k - 1 $.

exact.text:
Determine the least positive integer $k$ such that there exists a partition of $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ into $k$ disjoint subsets (colours) and a function $f: \mathbb{Z}_{>0} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ satisfying:
(i) If $m$ and $n$ belong to the same subset, then $f(m+n)=f(m)+f(n)$.
(ii) There exist $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that $f(m+n) \neq f(m)+f(n)$.

paraphrase.text:
Determine the minimal number $ k $ such that there exists a partition of $ \mathbb{Z}_{>0} $ into $ k $ sets and a mapping $ f: \mathbb{Z}_{>0} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_{>0} $ satisfying:
(i) For all $ m, n $ in the same set, $ f(m+n) = f(m) + f(n) $.
(ii) There exist $ m, n $ with $ f(m+n) \neq f(m) + f(n) $.

style.text:
Determine the minimal number $ k $ such that it is possible to assign each positive integer a label from a set of $ k $ labels and define a function $ f: \mathbb{Z}_{>0} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_{>0} $ satisfying:
(i) If two positive integers $ x $ and $ y $ have the same label, then $ f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) $.
(ii) There exist two positive integers $ x $ and $ y $ for which $ f(x + y) \neq f(x) + f(y) $.

paraphrase.text:
En un espacio euclidiano de tres dimensiones se designan por $e_{x}, e_{y}, e_{z}$ los tres vectores unitarios ortogonales sobre los ejes $x, y, z$, respectivamente.
a) Probar que el punto $R(s)=(1-s) e_{x}+(2-3 s) e_{y}+(2 s-1) e_{z}$, donde $s$ toma todos los valores reales, describe una recta (que designaremos por $M$ ).
b) ¿Qué describe el punto $S(s)=\left(1-s^{2}ight) e_{x}+\left(2-3 s^{2}ight) e_{y}+\left(2 s^{2}-1ight) e_{z}$ si $s$ toma todos los valores reales?
c) Hallar un vector paralelo a $M$.
d) ¿Para qué valores de $s$ está el punto $R(s)$ sobre el plano $2 x+3 y+2 z+1=0$ ?
e) Hallar la ecuación cartesiana del plano paralelo al anterior y que contenga el punto $R(3)$.
f) Hallar la ecuación cartesiana del plano perpendicular a $M$ que contenga el punto $R(2)$.

style.text:
Sea $v_{x}, v_{y}, v_{z}$ una base ortonormal en un espacio vectorial euclidiano de dimensión 3.
\na) Mostrar que el punto $R(s)=(2-s) v_{x} + (1-3s) v_{y} + (2s - 3) v_{z}$, con $s$ un número real cualquiera, describe una recta (llamada $M$).
\nb) ¿Qué describe el punto $S(s)=\left(2-s^{2}\right) v_{x} + \left(1-3s^{2}\right) v_{y} + \left(2s^{2} - 3\right) v_{z}$ si $s$ toma todos los valores reales?
\nc) Determinar un vector paralelo a $M$.
\nd) ¿Para qué valores de $s$ está el punto $R(s)$ sobre el plano $3x + 2y + 4z - 5 = 0$?
\ne) Hallar la ecuación cartesiana del plano paralelo al anterior y que contenga el punto $R(-1)$.
\nf) Hallar la ecuación cartesiana del plano perpendicular a $M$ que contenga el punto $R(0)$.

exact.text:
Sean $x$, $y$ y $z$ las longitudes de los lados de un triángulo. Demostrar que
$$\nx^{2} y(x-y) + y^{2} z(y-z) + z^{2} x(z-x) \geq 0
$$
Determinar en qué casos se cumple la igualdad.

paraphrase.text:
Sean $x$, $y$ y $z$ las longitudes de los lados de un triángulo. Demostrar que
$$\nx^{2} y(x-y) + y^{2} z(y-z) + z^{2} x(z-x) \geq 0
$$
Determinar en qué casos se cumple la igualdad.

style.text:
Sean $x$, $y$ y $z$ las longitudes de los lados de un triángulo. Demostrar que
$$\nx^{2} y(x-y) + y^{2} z(y-z) + z^{2} x(z-x) \geq 0
$$
Encontrar los casos de igualdad.

exact.text: Sean $x, y, z$ y $w$ enteros impares con $0 < x < y < z < w$ y $x w = y z$. Probar que si $x + w = 2^{n}$ y $y + z = 2^{p}$ para algunos enteros $n$ y $p$, entonces $x = 1$.

paraphrase.text: Sean $p, q, r$ y $s$ enteros impares tales que $0<p<q<r<s$ y $p s = q r$. Demostrar que si $p + s = 2^{n}$ y $q + r = 2^{l}$ para ciertos enteros $n$ y $l$, entonces $p = 1$.

style.text: Sean $p, q, r$ y $s$ enteros impares positivos tales que $p < q < r < s$ y $ps = qr$. Demostrar que si $p + s = 2^k$ y $q + r = 2^m$ para enteros $k$ y $m$, entonces $p = 1$.

exact.text:
Sea $D$ la suma de las longitudes de todas las diagonales de un polígono convexo plano con $k$ lados $(k>3)$, y sea $P$ su perímetro. Demostrar que
$$
 k-3<\frac{2D}{P}<\left[\frac{k}{2}\right]\left[\frac{k+1}{2}\right]-2
$$\nsiendo $[x]$ la parte entera de $x$.

paraphrase.text:
Sea $D$ la suma de las longitudes de todas las diagonales de un polígono convexo plano de $n$ vértices $(n > 3)$, y sea $L$ su perímetro. Probar que
$$
 n-3 < \frac{2D}{L} < \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n+1}{2} \right\rfloor - 2
$$\nsiendo $[x]$ la parte entera de $x$.

style.text:
Sea $s$ la suma de las longitudes de todas las diagonales de un polígono convexo con $m$ lados $(m>3)$, y sea $L$ su perímetro. Demostrar que
$$
 m-3<\frac{2s}{L}<\left[\frac{m}{2}\right]\left[\frac{m+1}{2}\right]-2
$$\nsiendo $[x]$ la parte entera de $x$.

exact.text: Sea $\mathcal{M}$ un conjunto de 1985 enteros positivos distintos, tales que todos tienen solamente factores primos entre 2 y 23. Probar que $\mathcal{M}$ contiene al menos un subconjunto de cuatro elementos distintos cuyo producto es una cuarta potencia perfecta.

paraphrase.text: Sea $\mathcal{A}$ un conjunto de 1985 enteros positivos distintos, tales que todos tienen únicamente factores primos menores o iguales a 26. Probar que $\mathcal{A}$ tiene al menos un subconjunto de cuatro elementos distintos cuyo producto es un número entero elevado a la cuarta potencia.

style.text: Sea $\mathcal{S}$ un conjunto de 1985 números enteros positivos distintos, tales que todos tienen factores primos menores o iguales a 26. Probar que existe un subconjunto de $\mathcal{S}$ con cuatro elementos cuyo producto es un cuadrado perfecto al cuadrado.

exact.text:
Demostrar que, dados siete números reales arbitrarios, existen dos entre ellos, $x$ y $y$, tales que
$$
\sqrt{3}|x-y| < |1 + x y|
$$
Proporcionar un conjunto de seis números reales para los cuales la propiedad no se cumple.

paraphrase.text: Probar que, para cualquier conjunto de siete números reales, existen dos números $x$ y $y$ tales que $$\sqrt{3}|x - y| < |1 + xy|$$ Proporcionar un conjunto de seis números reales para los cuales esto no se cumple.

style.text: Sea $S$ un conjunto de siete números reales. Probar que existen dos números $x$ y $y$ en $S$ tales que $$\sqrt{3}|x - y| < |1 + xy|$$ Mostrar un ejemplo de un conjunto de seis números reales donde esta desigualdad no se cumple para ningún par.

paraphrase.text:
Sean $c$ y $d$ enteros distintos de $0$, $1$ y $-1$, y consideremos la matriz
$$
\left(
\begin{array}{ccccc}\nc+d & c+d^{2} & c+d^{3} & \ldots & c+d^{m} \\\nc^{2}+d & c^{2}+d^{2} & c^{2}+d^{3} & \ldots & c^{2}+d^{m} \\\nc^{3}+d & c^{3}+d^{2} & c^{3}+d^{3} & \ldots & c^{3}+d^{m} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\\nc^{n}+d & c^{n}+d^{2} & c^{n}+d^{3} & \ldots & c^{n}+d^{m}
\end{array}
\right)
$$
Encontrar un subconjunto $S$ de filas de la matriz, con la menor cantidad posible, tal que cualquier otra fila pueda escribirse como combinación lineal, con coeficientes enteros, de las filas de $S$. Mostrar cómo expresar cada fila en términos de $S$.

style.text:
Sean $x$ y $y$ enteros diferentes de $0$, $1$ y $-1$, y consideremos la matriz
$$
\left(
\begin{array}{ccccc}
 x+y & x+y^{2} & x+y^{3} & \ldots & x+y^{m} \\
 x^{2}+y & x^{2}+y^{2} & x^{2}+y^{3} & \ldots & x^{2}+y^{m} \\
 x^{3}+y & x^{3}+y^{2} & x^{3}+y^{3} & \ldots & x^{3}+y^{m} \\
 \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\
 x^{n}+y & x^{n}+y^{2} & x^{n}+y^{3} & \ldots & x^{n}+y^{m}
\end{array}
\right)
$$
Determinar un subconjunto $S$ de filas de esa matriz, lo menor posible, tal que cualquier otra fila se pueda expresar como suma de las filas de $S$ multiplicadas por números enteros apropiados (es decir, como combinación lineal con coeficientes enteros de las filas de $S$). Explicitar dichas combinaciones lineales.

exact.text: Mostrar que para cualquier número primo $p$ con $p \neq 2$ y $p \neq 5$, existen infinitos múltiplos de $p$ cuyas cifras son todas 1.

paraphrase.text: Mostrar que si $p$ es un número primo distinto de 2 y de 5, entonces existen infinitos múltiplos de $p$ compuestos únicamente por la cifra 1.

style.text: Probar que para cada número primo $q \neq 2, 5$, existe una infinidad de enteros positivos $n$ tales que $\underbrace{11\ldots1}_{n \text{ veces}}$ es divisible por $q$.

exact.text: En una caja hay 900 cartas con números del 100 al 999. Se extraen cartas aleatoriamente (sin reemplazo) y se calcula la suma de los dígitos de cada carta extraída. ¿Cuál es el número mínimo de cartas que se deben sacar para asegurar que tres de estas sumas sean idénticas?

paraphrase.text: En una caja hay 900 cartas con números del 100 al 999. Se eligen aleatoriamente (sin repetición) cartas y se calcula la suma de los dígitos de cada una. ¿Cuál es el número mínimo de cartas que se deben seleccionar para asegurar que al menos tres de estas sumas coincidan?

style.text: En una urna hay 900 fichas, cada una marcada con un número entre 100 y 999. Se extraen fichas al azar (sin devolución) y se calcula la suma de los dígitos de cada número extraído. ¿Cuál es el número mínimo de fichas que deben sacarse para estar seguros de que al menos tres de esas sumas sean idénticas?

exact.text:
Sea $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ una función definida para todo $s, n \in \mathbb{N}$ mediante las siguientes reglas:

$f(1)=f\left(2^{s}\right)=1$ y $f\left(2^{s}+n\right)=f(n)+1$ si $n < 2^{s}$.

Encontrar el valor máximo de $f(n)$ para $n \leq 2001$.

Determinar el menor $n$ tal que $f(n)=2001$.

paraphrase.text: Sea $g: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ una función definida sobre el conjunto de los números naturales $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ tal que $g(1)=g(2^{k})=1$ para todo $k \in \mathbb{N}$, y si $m < 2^{k}$, entonces $g(2^{k} + m) = g(m) + 1$. Determinar el valor máximo de $g(n)$ para $n \leq 2001$. Hallar el menor $n$ para el cual $g(n) = 2001$.

style.text: Definir la función $ g: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N} $ tal que $ g(1) = g\left(2^{k}\right) = 1 $ para cualquier $ k \in \mathbb{N} $, y si $ m < 2^{k} $, entonces $ g\left(2^{k}+m\right) = g(m)+1 $. Determinar el valor máximo de $ g(n) $ para $ n \leq 2001 $. Encontrar el menor número natural $ n $ tal que $ g(n) = 2001 $.

exact.text: Dado un arreglo $3 \times 3$ con los números del $1$ al $9$ distribuidos una vez cada uno, se forman seis números de tres dígitos: tres corresponden a las filas leídas de izquierda a derecha, y tres corresponden a las columnas leídas de arriba hacia abajo. ¿Es posible que la suma total de estos seis números sea igual a $2001$?

paraphrase.text: Se colocan los dígitos del $1$ al $9$ en una cuadrícula de $3 \times 3$. A continuación, se forman tres números horizontales y tres números verticales, cada uno de tres dígitos, y se suman estos seis números. ¿Es posible que esta suma total sea igual a $2001$?

style.text: Los dígitos del $1$ al $9$ se colocan una vez cada uno en una cuadrícula de $3 \times 3$. Luego se forman seis números de tres dígitos: tres de las filas y tres de las columnas. ¿Es posible que la suma de estos seis números sea igual a $2001$?

exact.text: Los lados de un triángulo forman una sucesión geométrica con ratio $r$. Determina los valores de $r$ que corresponden a triángulos acutángulos, rectángulos y obtusángulos.

paraphrase.text: Un triángulo tiene lados cuyas medidas forman una progresión geométrica con factor $r$. Determina los posibles valores de $r$ para los cuales el triángulo es acutángulo, rectángulo y obtusángulo.

style.text: Los lados de un triángulo tienen longitudes $a$, $ar$ y $ar^2$, con $a > 0$. Determina los valores de $r$ que hacen que el triángulo sea, respectivamente, acutángulo, rectángulo o obtusángulo.

exact.text:
Encontrar todos los polinomios $P(t)$ tales que
$$
\quad P\left((x+y)(x-y)\right)=P(x+y) P(x-y)
$$\npara todo $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

paraphrase.text:
Encuentra todos los polinomios $Q(t)$ en una variable tales que
$$
Q\left(a^{2}-b^{2}\right)=Q(a+b) Q(a-b)
$$\npara todo $a$ y $b$ reales.

style.text:
Determinar todos los polinomios $Q(z)$ tales que
$$
Q\left(a^{2}-b^{2}\right)=Q(a+b) Q(a-b)
$$\npara todos los números reales $a$ y $b$.

exact.text: Dado un arreglo lineal de $2n$ bolas blancas y $2n$ bolas negras, muestra que existe un subarreglo contiguo con exactamente $n$ bolas blancas y $n$ bolas negras, independientemente del orden inicial.

paraphrase.text: Dado un arreglo lineal de $2n$ bolas blancas y $2n$ bolas negras, demuestra que existe un subarreglo continuo que contiene exactamente $n$ bolas blancas y $n$ bolas negras, sin importar el orden inicial.

exact.text: ¿Hay algún número $2^n$, con $n \in \mathbb{N}$, cuya representación decimal no contenga ningún dígito cero y cuyos dígitos puedan reordenarse para formar un número $2^m$ con $m \in \mathbb{N}$ y $m \neq n$? Justificar la respuesta.

paraphrase.text: ¿Existe algún entero $n$ tal que $2^n$ tenga únicamente dígitos no nulos en su representación decimal, y los dígitos puedan reordenarse para formar una representación decimal distinta que también sea una potencia de $2$? Justificar la respuesta.

style.text: ¿Hay algún número de la forma $2^n$ (con $n \in \mathbb{N}$) cuyos dígitos en base $10$ no contengan ningún cero, y tal que al reordenar dichos dígitos se obtenga otro número de la forma $2^m$ con $m \neq n$? Justificar la respuesta.

exact.text:
Encontrar todas las soluciones enteras posibles, $x$ e $y$, de la ecuación:
$$\nq x + q y = x y
$$\nsiendo $q$ un cierto número primo.

paraphrase.text:
Determinar todos los pares de enteros $(a, b)$ tales que:
$$\nq(a + b) = ab
$$\ndonde $q$ es un número primo.

style.text: Determinar todos los enteros $a$ y $b$ que satisfacen la ecuación $$ q(a + b) = ab $$ donde $q$ es un número primo.

exact.text: Sea $ p \geq 3 $ un número primo. Se trazan segmentos desde puntos que dividen cada lado de un triángulo en $ p $ segmentos iguales hasta el vértice opuesto. Calcula el máximo número de regiones no superpuestas que se forman en el interior del triángulo.

paraphrase.text: Sea $ p \geq 3 $ un número primo. Se trazan segmentos desde cada punto de división de los lados de un triángulo (divididos en $ p $ partes iguales) hacia el vértice opuesto. Encuentra el número máximo de regiones disjuntas en las que se divide el triángulo.

style.text: Sea $ p $ un número primo mayor que 2. Si se trazan segmentos que conectan los puntos que dividen a cada lado de un triángulo en $ p $ segmentos congruentes con el vértice opuesto, ¿cuál es el número máximo de regiones no superpuestas que se forman dentro del triángulo?

exact.text: Hallar $2\sum_{k=1}^{2008} h\left(\frac{k}{2009}\right)$, con $h(t)=\frac{5}{5+25^{t}}$ y $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

paraphrase.text: Hallar el valor de $2\sum_{k=1}^{2008} h\left(\frac{k}{2009}\right)$, donde $$ h(t)=\frac{5}{5+25^{t}}, \quad t \in \mathbb{R} $$

style.text: Sea $g(x) = \frac{5}{5+25^{x}}$, calcule $2\left[g\left(\frac{1}{2009}\right)+g\left(\frac{2}{2009}\right)+\ldots+g\left(\frac{2008}{2009}\right)\right]$.

exact.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo con $n > 1$. Determinar todos los pares enteros $(a, b)$ tales que $x^{n} + a x - 2008 = 0$ y $x^{n} + b x - 2009 = 0$ comparten al menos una solución real común.

paraphrase.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo mayor que $1$. Determinar todos los pares $(a, b)$ de enteros para los cuales las ecuaciones $x^{n} + a x - 2008 = 0$ y $x^{n} + b x - 2009 = 0$ comparten al menos una solución real común.

style.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo mayor que $1$. Encontrar todos los pares $(a, b)$ de enteros tales que las ecuaciones $x^{n} + a x - 2008 = 0$ y $x^{n} + b x - 2009 = 0$ compartan al menos una solución real común.

exact.text: Dado el polinomio cuadrático $ p(x) = a x^{2} + b x + c $ con $a \neq 0$ y raíces distintas $x_{1}$ y $x_{2}$, demuestra que $p\left(x_{1}^{3}\right) = p\left(x_{2}^{3}\right)$ si y solo si $a^{2} + 3 a c - b^{2} = 0$. ¿Es esta condición necesaria?

paraphrase.text: Sea $q(x) = d x^{2} + e x + f$, $(d \neq 0)$, un polinomio cuadrático con raíces $y_{1}$ y $y_{2}$ distintas. Justifica que $q\left(y_{1}^{3}\right) = q\left(y_{2}^{3}\right)$ implica que $d^{2} + 3 d f - e^{2} = 0$. ¿Es esta condición necesaria?

style.text: Sea $ q(x) = m x^{2} + n x + p $, con $ m \neq 0 $, cuyas soluciones $ \alpha $ y $ \beta $ son distintas. Justifica que para que $ q(\alpha^{3}) = q(\beta^{3}) $ es suficiente que $ m^{2} + 3 m p - n^{2} = 0 $. ¿Es también necesaria esta condición?

exact.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Determine the total of all integers less than $10n$ that are relatively prime to $10$.

paraphrase.text: Given a positive integer $n$, compute the total of all positive integers less than $10n$ that are coprime with $10$.

style.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Compute the total of all natural numbers less than $10n$ that are relatively prime to $10$.

exact.text: Suppose $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are real monic cubic polynomials. Is it possible for the composition $P(Q(x))$ to have nine distinct nonnegative integer roots with a total sum of 72?

paraphrase.text: Can we find real monic cubic polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ such that the composite function $P(Q(x))$ has nine distinct nonnegative integer roots whose total sum is 72?

style.text: Can we find two monic cubic polynomials $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ with real coefficients such that the equation $A(B(x)) = 0$ has nine distinct nonnegative integer roots whose total sum is 72?

exact.text: Sea $\Gamma$ una circunferencia con diámetro $XY$ y $N$ el punto medio del arco $XY$ que no contiene el centro. Sean $A$ y $B$ puntos sobre $XY$, y sean $C$ y $D$ las segundas intersecciones de $NA$ y $NB$ con $\Gamma$. Sean $P$ la intersección de las tangentes a $\Gamma$ en $C$ y $D$. Sea $M$ la intersección de $NP$ con $XY$. Probar que $M$ es el punto medio de $AB$.

paraphrase.text: Sean $A$, $B$ puntos en el diámetro $XY$ de una circunferencia $\Gamma$, y $N$ el punto medio del arco $XY$ que no contiene a $A$ ni $B$. Sean $C$ y $D$ las segundas intersecciones de las rectas $NA$ y $NB$ con $\Gamma$. Si las tangentes en $C$ y $D$ a $\Gamma$ se cortan en $P$, y $M$ es la intersección de $NP$ con $XY$, probar que $M$ es el punto medio de $AB$.

style.text: Sea $\Gamma$ una circunferencia con diámetro $XY$, y sea $N$ el punto medio del arco $XY$ que no contiene al punto $A$ ni $B$. Sean $A$ y $B$ puntos sobre $XY$. Sean $C$ y $D$ las segundas intersecciones de $NA$ y $NB$ con $\Gamma$, respectivamente. Sean $P$ el punto de intersección de las tangentes a $\Gamma$ en $C$ y $D$, y $M$ el punto donde $NP$ corta a $XY$. Probar que $M$ es el punto medio de $AB$.

exact.text:
Sea $P$ un conjunto de $4027$ puntos en el plano, con $2013$ puntos rojos y $2014$ azules, y ningún subconjunto de tres puntos colineales. Decimos que un conjunto de rectas es "bueno" si:
* ninguna recta contiene a ningún punto de $P$;
* cada región del plano definida por las rectas contiene únicamente puntos de un solo color.

Determinar el menor número $k$ tal que para cualquier $P$ como arriba existe un conjunto bueno de $k$ rectas.

paraphrase.text:
Dada una configuración de $4027$ puntos en el plano, con $2013$ puntos rojos y $2014$ puntos azules, y sin que haya tres puntos alineados, se define como colombiana. Se dibujan algunas rectas que dividen el plano en regiones. Una colección de rectas es buena para una configuración colombiana si:
* ninguna de las rectas pasa por algún punto;
* ninguna región contiene puntos de ambos colores.

Determinar el menor valor de $k$ tal que, para cualquier configuración colombiana, existe una colección buena de $k$ rectas.

style.text:
Sea $S$ un conjunto de $4027$ puntos en el plano, con $2013$ puntos de color rojo y $2014$ de color azul, y tal que ningún trio de puntos es colineal. Llamamos a $S$ una configuración de tipo $\alpha$. Una familia de rectas $\mathcal{R}$ se dice que separa colores si:
* ninguna recta en $\mathcal{R}$ pasa por algún punto de $S$;
* cada región definida por $\mathcal{R}$ contiene puntos de un único color.

Determinar el menor número $k$ tal que cualquier configuración $\alpha$ admite una familia separadora de $k$ rectas.

exact.text: Encontrar un polinomio de tercer grado cuyas raíces coincidan con los cuadrados de las raíces del polinomio $q(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + 3x + 4$.

paraphrase.text: Determinar un polinomio cúbico cuyas raíces sean los cuadrados de las raíces del polinomio $q(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + 3x + 4$.

style.text: Sea $q(x)$ un polinomio cuyas raíces son los cuadrados de las raíces de $r(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x + 4$. Determinar $q(x)$.

exact.text: Let $p, n$ be positive integers with $p$ prime and $p < n$. Given that $n+1 \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ and $\gcd\left(\left\lfloor\frac{n}{p}\right\rfloor, (p-1)!\right) = 1$, show that $p \cdot \left\lfloor\frac{n}{p}\right\rfloor^2$ divides $\binom{n}{p} - \left\lfloor\frac{n}{p}\right\rfloor$.

paraphrase.text: Let $q, m$ be positive integers such that $q$ is prime and $q < m$. If $q$ divides $m+1$ and $\left(\left[\frac{m}{q}\right], (q-1)!\right) = 1$, then prove that $q \cdot \left[\frac{m}{q}\right]^2$ divides $\binom{m}{q} - \left[\frac{m}{q}\right]$. (Here $[x]$ denotes the floor function of the real number $x$.)

style.text: Let $q, m$ be positive integers such that $q$ is prime and $q < m$. If $q$ divides $m+1$ and $\left(\left[\frac{m}{q}\right], (q-1)!\right) = 1$, then prove that $q \cdot \left[\frac{m}{q}\right]^2$ divides $\binom{m}{q} - \left[\frac{m}{q}\right]$. (Here $[x]$ represents the floor of the real number $x$.)

exact.text: Sea $S = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, m\}$ con $m > 5$. Demostrar que existe un conjunto finito $T$ de enteros positivos distintos tal que $S \subseteq T$ y se cumple $$\sum_{x \in T} x^2 = \prod_{x \in T} x.$$

paraphrase.text: Sea $S = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, k\}$ con $k > 5$. Demostrar que existe un conjunto finito $T$ de enteros positivos distintos tal que $S \subseteq T$ y $$\sum_{x \in T} x^2 = \prod_{x \in T} x.$$

style.text: \text{Sea } C = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, m\} \text{ con } m > 5. \text{Demostrar que existe un conjunto finito } D \text{ de enteros positivos distintos tal que } C \subseteq D \text{ y } \prod_{x \in D} x = \sum_{x \in D} x^2.

exact.text:
Let $a, b, c$ be positive numbers such that $a^2b^2 + b^2c^2 + c^2a^2 = 6abc$. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{\frac{a}{a + bc}} + \sqrt{\frac{b}{b + ca}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{c + ab}} \ge \sqrt{3}
$$

paraphrase.text:
Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers satisfying $a^2b^2 + b^2c^2 + c^2a^2 = 6abc$. Prove that
$$\sqrt{\frac{a}{a + bc}} + \sqrt{\frac{b}{b + ca}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{c + ab}} \ge \sqrt{3}$$

style.text: \text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be positive numbers such that } a^2b^2 + b^2c^2 + c^2a^2 = 6abc. \text{ Prove that} $$ \sqrt{\frac{a}{a + bc}} + \sqrt{\frac{b}{b + ca}} + \sqrt{\frac{c}{c + ab}} \ge \sqrt{3} $$

exact.text: \text{Show that there are no positive integer solutions to } 2^a + 21^a = b^3 \text{ and determine all nonnegative integer solutions to } 2^a + 21^b = c^2.

exact.text: Halla todas las funciones $f: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ tales que $f(n) + f(n+1) = 2n + 1$ para cada $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ y $\sum_{k=1}^{63} f(k) = 2015$

paraphrase.text:
Encuentra todas las funciones $ g: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z} $ que cumplen $ g(m) + g(m+1) = 2m+1 $ para cada entero $ m $ y

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{63} g(j) = 2015
$$

exact.text: Sea $T_n = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ con $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Determinar todos los $n$ tales que $\prod_{k=0}^{15} T_{n+k}$ es un cuadrado perfecto.

paraphrase.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo y defínase $T_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} k$. Determinar todos los enteros $n$ tales que el producto $T_n T_{n+1} \cdots T_{n+15}$ es un cuadrado perfecto.

style.text: Sea $T_k = \frac{k(k+1)}{2}$ el $k$-ésimo número triangular. Determinar todos los enteros positivos $m$ tales que el producto $T_m T_{m+1} \cdots T_{m+15}$ es un cuadrado perfecto.

exact.text: Sea $m$ un entero positivo. Sean $a$ y $b$ enteros positivos distintos tales que $m^2 < a, b < m^2 + m$. Determinar todos los divisores $d$ del producto $ab$ que satisfacen $m^2 < d < m^2 + m$.

paraphrase.text: Sea $n \ge 1$ un entero positivo. Sean $x$ y $y$ enteros positivos diferentes tales que $n^2 < x, y < n^2 + n$. Hallar todos los enteros $k$ que dividen a $xy$ y satisfacen $n^2 < k < n^2 + n$.

style.text: Sea $n \ge 1$ un número natural. Sean $p$ y $q$ enteros positivos tales que $n^2 < p < n^2 + n$ y $n^2 < q < n^2 + n$, con $p \ne q$. Determinar todos los enteros $k$ que dividen a $pq$ y satisfacen $n^2 < k < n^2 + n$.

exact.text: Las soluciones de $x^3 - 14x^2 + Bx - 84 = 0$ representan las longitudes de los lados de un triángulo rectángulo. Determinar el valor de $B$.

paraphrase.text: Sean $a$, $b$, y $c$ las raíces del polinomio $x^3 - 14x^2 + Bx - 84$, y supongamos que $a$, $b$, y $c$ forman los lados de un triángulo rectángulo. Determinar el valor de $B$.

style.text: Sean $a$, $b$, y $c$ las raíces del polinomio $x^3 - 14x^2 + Bx - 84$, donde $a$, $b$, y $c$ son las longitudes de los lados de un triángulo rectángulo. Determinar el valor de $B$.

exact.text:
Sean $p, q, r$ números primos distintos. Probar que
$$
(p q)^{r-1} + (q r)^{p-1} + (r p)^{q-1} - 1
$$\nes divisible por $p q r$.

paraphrase.text: Sean $p, q, r$ números primos distintos. Probar que $$ (p q)^{r-1} + (q r)^{p-1} + (r p)^{q-1} - 1 $$ es divisible por $p q r$.

$$\nes divisible por $p q r$.

exact.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo. Demostrar que si $7^n$ termina en 3, entonces su segunda cifra desde la derecha es 4.

paraphrase.text: Sea $n$ un entero positivo. Demostrar que si al elevar $7$ a la potencia $n$ se obtiene un número cuyo dígito de las unidades es 3, entonces el dígito de las decenas es 4.

exact.text: Determinar si existe un conjunto finito $ P $ de números primos positivos tal que, para todo entero $ n \geq 2 $, la suma $ \sum_{k=2}^{n} k^{2} $ sea divisible por al menos un número en $ P $.

paraphrase.text: Decidir si existe un conjunto finito $ T $ compuesto por primos positivos tal que para cada entero $ m \geq 2 $, la suma $ 2^{2} + 3^{2} + \cdots + m^{2} $ sea divisible por al menos un elemento de $ T $.

exact.text:
Encuentre todas las ternas reales $(x, y, z)$ tales que
$$
\begin{array}{cccc}
 x+y+z & = & 1 \\
 x y(x - y) + y z(y - z) + z x(z - x) & = & 0 \\
 x^{3} - y^{3} + y^{2} - z^{2} + z - x & = & 0
\end{array}
$$

\begin{array}{cccc}
 a+b+c & = & 1 \\
 a^{2} b + b^{2} c + c^{2} a & = & a b^{2} + b c^{2} + c a^{2} \\
 a^{3} + b^{2} + c & = & b^{3} + c^{2} + a
\end{array}
$$

exact.text:
Sean $x, y, z, w$ números reales positivos tales que
$$\nx+y+\frac{1}{xy}=z+w+\frac{1}{zw} \quad \text{y} \quad \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+xy=\frac{1}{z}+\frac{1}{w}+zw.
$$
Prueba que al menos dos de $x, y, z, w$ son iguales.

$$
Prueba que al menos dos de $x, y, p, q$ son iguales.

exact.text:
Sea $n = 203$. Inicialmente, la primera casilla contiene $n$ fichas y el resto están vacías. En cada movimiento, se puede:
* Mover una ficha a una casilla vecina (izquierda o derecha), o
* Mover exactamente $20$ fichas de una casilla a una adyacente (en una dirección).
Después de $n + 2020$ movimientos, cada casilla tiene exactamente una ficha. Demuestra que al menos una ficha ha sido desplazada a la izquierda al menos nueve veces.

paraphrase.text:
Sea una fila de $ n = 203 $ casillas, con inicialmente $ n $ fichas en la primera casilla y el resto vacías. En cada paso se puede:
* Mover una ficha a una casilla contigua (izquierda o derecha), o
* Mover exactamente $ 20 $ fichas de una casilla a una casilla contigua (todas a la izquierda o todas a la derecha).
Después de $ m = 2023 $ movimientos, cada casilla contiene exactamente una ficha. Demuestra que hay al menos una ficha que ha sido movida hacia la izquierda un mínimo de nueve veces.

style.text:
En una hilera de 203 posiciones, la posición más a la izquierda tiene 203 piedras y las restantes están vacías. En cada paso, se puede:
* Mover una piedra a una posición vecina (izquierda o derecha), o
* Mover exactamente 20 piedras de una posición a una posición adyacente (todas a la izquierda o todas a la derecha).
Después de 2023 movimientos, hay exactamente una piedra en cada posición. Prueba que hay al menos una piedra que se movió a la izquierda al menos nueve veces.
