paraphrase.text: Poiščite naravno število $n > 1$, za katero je izraz $$\frac{\prod_{k=2}^n \log_{10} k}{10^{n-1}}$$ minimalen. Katera je minimalna vrednost?

style.text: \text{Za katera naravna števila } m > 1 \text{ doseže izraz} \quad \frac{\prod_{k=2}^m \log_{10} k}{10^{m-1}} \quad \text{najmanjšo vrednost? Kolikšna je ta vrednost?}

exact.text: Jaka ima trimestno število $x$, v katerem so vse števke različne in neničelne. Nato je narisal vse možne trimestna števila, ki jih lahko sestavi z enakimi števkami, kot jih ima $x$. Poišči vsa števila $x$, če je vsota vseh teh števil enaka $3434$.

paraphrase.text: Jaka je izbral tremestno število $x$ s tremi različnimi neničelnimi števkami. Nato je zapisal vsa možna tremestna števila, ki jih je mogoče zapisati z enakimi števkami kot $x$. Določi vse možne vrednosti $x$, če je vsota teh števil enaka $3434$.

style.text: Ana je izbrala trimestno število $a$ s tremi različnimi neničelnimi števkami. Nato je zapisala vsa druga trimestna števila, ki jih lahko sestavi s temi števkami. Določi vse možne števila $a$, če je vsota vseh zapisanih števil enaka $3434$.

exact.text: Let $N = 12k$ be the number of villagers. Each person is acquainted with $3k + 6$ others, and acquaintances are mutual. For any two villagers, there is a fixed number $n$ of villagers who know both. Find $N$.

paraphrase.text: A community of $12k$ members is such that each member is connected to $3k + 6$ others in a symmetric relationship. There is a positive integer $n$ for which any pair of members shares exactly $n$ mutual connections. Determine the total number of members in the community.

style.text: A social network has $12k$ users, and each user is friends with $3k + 6$ others. All friendships are mutual. For any two users, the number of mutual friends they share is a constant $n$. What is the total number of users in the network?

exact.text: Naj bo $S$ neprazna množica naravnih števil, kjer za vsaka $x$ in $y$ iz $S$ velja, da $x$ deli $y$ ali $y$ deli $x$. Dokaži, da je vsako $z$ iz $S$ večje od vsote vseh števil iz $S$, ki so strogo manjša od $z$.

paraphrase.text: Naj bo $S$ neprazna množica naravnih števil, kjer za vsaka dva elementa $x$ in $y$ velja, da $x$ deli $y$ ali obratno. Dokaži, da velja $x > \sum_{\substack{y \in S \ y < x}} y$ za vsak $x \in S$.

style.text: Naj bo $S$ množica naravnih števil, kjer za vsaka dva elementa $x$ in $y$ velja $x \mid y$ ali $y \mid x$. Pokaži, da je vsak element $z$ iz $S$ večji od vsote vseh elementov iz $S$, ki so strogo manjši od $z$.

exact.text: Let $n = (p^2 - 4)(p^2 - 1) + 9$. If $p$ is a prime number, determine the minimum digit sum of $n$ and all primes $p$ that achieve it.

paraphrase.text: Given $n = (p^2 - 1)(p^2 - 4) + 9$ with $p$ a prime, determine the smallest digit sum of $n$ and identify all primes $p$ for which this minimum is achieved.

style.text: Let $n = (q^2 - 4)(q^2 - 1) + 9$. If $q$ is a prime number, find the smallest possible digit sum of $n$ and all such primes $q$ that achieve it.

exact.text: Let $x$ be a real number such that $1 + x + \frac{1}{x}$ is a positive integer. Prove that $1 + x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2}$ is a positive integer divisible by $1 + x + \frac{1}{x}$.

paraphrase.text: Let $x$ be a real number such that $x + \frac{1}{x} + 1$ is a positive integer $n$. Prove that $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 1$ is an integer divisible by $n$.

style.text: Let $a$ be a real number such that $a + \frac{1}{a} + 1$ is a positive integer. Prove that $a^2 + \frac{1}{a^2} + 1$ is a positive integer divisible by $a + \frac{1}{a} + 1$.

exact.text: Za katere naravne števila $n$ obstaja celo število $k$ takšno, da je $13k$ in vsota števk $13k$ enaka $n$?

paraphrase.text: Za katere pozitivne cele število $n$ obstaja število oblike $13k$, kjer je $k$ naravno število, z vsoto števk $n$?

style.text: Za katera naravna števila $k$ obstaja večkratnik števila $13$, katerega vsota števk je enaka $k$?

exact.text: Trije igralci: A, B in C so trikrat igrali poker. V vsaki igri je izgubilec plačal drugima igralcema dvakrat toliko denarja, kot so imeli trenutno. Prvič je izgubil A, drugič B in tretjič C. Na koncu je vsak imel 24 evrov. Kdo je izgubil največ in koliko?

paraphrase.text: Tri osebe, A, B in C, so trikrat igrale poker. Prvič je izgubil A in mora plačati B in C vsakemu toliko, kot imata na začetku igre. Drugič je izgubil B in mora plačati A in C vsakemu toliko, kot imata trenutno. Tretjič je izgubil C in plača A in B na enak način. Na koncu vsak ima 24 evrov. Kdo je izgubil največ in koliko?

style.text: Ana, Ben in Ciril so trikrat igrali kartologijo. Prvič je izgubila Ana in zato mora plačati Benju in Cirilu, vsakemu posebej toliko, kot imata na začetku igre. Drugič izgubi Ben in plačuje Ani in Cirilu, vsakemu toliko, kot imata trenutno. Tretjič izgubi Ciril in plačuje Ani in Benju na enak način. Po treh igrah ima vsak 24 evrov. Kdo je izgubil največ in koliko?

exact.text: Naj bo $ ab $ dvomestno število, kjer je $ a $ števka desetic in $ b $ števka enic. Če med $ a $ in $ b $ vrinemo 0, dobimo število $ a0b $. Če $ a0b = 9 \cdot ab $, poišči vse možne $ ab $.

paraphrase.text: Če v dvomestno število vmes vstavimo števko 0, dobimo število, ki je devetkrat večje. Katera so vsa taka dvomestna števila?

style.text: Dvomestno število je bilo razširjeno z vstavljanjem številke $ 0 $ med njegovi števki, in rezultat je bil devetkrat večji. Poišči vsa taka izvirna števila.

exact.text: Determine all integer values of $x$ such that $9x^2 - 40x + 39$ is equal to $p^k$, where $p$ is a prime and $k$ is a non-negative integer.

paraphrase.text: Determine all integers $n$ for which $9n^2 - 40n + 39$ equals $q^b$, where $q$ is a prime and $b$ is a non-negative integer.

style.text: Find all integers $ y $, such that $ 9y^2 - 40y + 39 $ is equal to $ q^b $, where $ q $ is a prime and $ b $ is a non-negative integer.

exact.text: Naj bosta $a$ in $b$ celi števili, za kateri velja $a + a b + b^{2} = 1$ in $b(5 + a) \geq 0$. Katerim celim številom je lahko enaka vrednost izraza $a - b$?

paraphrase.text: Naj bosta $a$ in $b$ celi števili, za kateri velja $a + a b + b^{2} = 1$ in $b(5 + a) \geq 0$. Katerim celim številom je lahko enaka vrednost izraza $a - b$?

style.text: Določi vse možne cele vrednosti izraza $a - b$, če velja $a + a b + b^{2} = 1$ in $b(5 + a) \geq 0$.

exact.text: Let $ABCD$ be a tangential quadrilateral with an incircle tangent to $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ at points $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$, respectively. Suppose the extensions of $AB$ and $CD$ meet at $E$, and the extensions of $AD$ and $BC$ meet at $F$. Let $I_1$ be the intersection of the angle bisectors of $\angle QPS$ and $\angle PSR$, and let $I_2$ be the intersection of the angle bisectors of $\angle RQP$ and $\angle SRQ$. Prove that $AC$, $EF$, and $I_1I_2$ are either concurrent or parallel.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABCD$ be a tangential quadrilateral with an incircle tangent to $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ at points $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$, respectively. Let $E$ be the intersection of lines $AB$ and $CD$, and let $F$ be the intersection of lines $AD$ and $BC$. Let $I_1$ be the intersection of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle QPS$ and $\angle PSR$, and $I_2$ the intersection of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle RQP$ and $\angle SRQ$. Show that the lines $AC$, $EF$, and $I_1I_2$ are either concurrent or parallel.

style.text: Let $PQRS$ be a tangential quadrilateral with an incircle touching sides $PQ$, $QR$, $RS$, and $SP$ at points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, respectively. Let the lines $PQ$ and $RS$ intersect at point $E$, and let the lines $PS$ and $QR$ intersect at point $F$. Let $I_1$ be the intersection of the angle bisectors of $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ACD$, and let $I_2$ be the intersection of the angle bisectors of $\angle CBA$ and $\angle DCA$. Prove that the lines $BD$, $EF$, and $I_1I_2$ either intersect at a common point or are parallel.

exact.text: Find all positive integers $n$ and prime numbers $p$ such that $n + \frac{2}{p}$ is a perfect $n$th power of an integer.

paraphrase.text: Find all positive integers $k$ and prime numbers $q$ such that $\sqrt[k]{k + \frac{2}{q}}$ is an integer.

style.text: Find all positive integers $a$ and prime numbers $q$ such that $\sqrt[a]{a+\frac{2}{q}}$ is an integer.

exact.text: Two players, Lara and Sara, take turns drawing $n$ straight lines on a rectangular sheet of paper, with one line per turn. Each line is drawn from one edge to the opposite edge and is parallel to either of the edges. Lines cannot overlap with the edges or with each other. The game ends when $n$ lines are drawn, and the number of rectangles formed on the sheet is counted. Lara wins if the number is odd, and Sara wins if it is even. Determine who wins the game depending on $n$ and who draws the first line.

paraphrase.text: Two players, Lara and Sara, alternately draw $n$ straight lines on a rectangle. Each line is drawn from one side to the opposite side and is parallel to one of the rectangle's sides. No line coincides with a side or another line. After all lines are drawn, the rectangle is partitioned into smaller rectangles. Lara wins if the number of these smaller rectangles is odd, and Sara wins if it is even. Determine who wins, based on $n$ and who draws the first line.

style.text: Alice and Bob take turns drawing $n$ lines on a rectangular board, one at a time. Each line is horizontal or vertical and spans the full length or height of the board. Lines cannot coincide with the edges or with previously drawn lines. The board is then partitioned into multiple smaller rectangles. If the total number of these rectangles is odd, Alice wins; if it is even, Bob wins. Determine the winner depending on $n$ and who begins the game.

exact.text: The numbers $1$ to $33$ are written on a board. In each operation, we pick two numbers where one divides the other. After removing these two, we write the result of dividing the larger by the smaller. This is repeated until no such pair remains. What is the minimum number of numbers that can remain on the board?

paraphrase.text: A set of numbers from $1$ to $33$ is written on a board. In each operation, we pick two numbers where one is a multiple of the other, erase them, and write their quotient in their place. This is repeated until no such pair exists. What is the minimum number of numbers that can remain on the board?

style.text: Numbers $a_1 = 1$, $a_2 = 2$, $\ldots$, $a_{33} = 33$ are written on a board. In each move, we pick two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x \mid y$, erase them, and write $\frac{y}{x}$ in their place. This continues until no such pair exists. What is the minimum number of numbers that can remain on the board?

exact.text: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers such that $n > m \ge 1$. Consider the set $S = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{N}^2 \mid 1 \le x, y \le n\}$. Find the smallest natural number $k$ such that for every subset $P \subseteq S$ with $|P| = k$, there exist $m+1$ elements $(x_1, y_1), \dots, (x_{m+1}, y_{m+1})$ in $P$ with all $x_i$ distinct and all $y_i$ distinct.

paraphrase.text: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers with $b > a \ge 1$. Define $T$ as the set of all pairs $(p, q)$ with $1 \le p, q \le b$. Find the smallest integer $k$ such that any subset $Q \subseteq T$ with $|Q| = k$ contains $a+1$ pairs $(p_1, q_1), (p_2, q_2), \dots, (p_{a+1}, q_{a+1})$ where all the $p_i$ are distinct and all the $q_i$ are distinct.

style.text: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $n > m$. Consider the grid $[n] \times [n]$, where $[n] = \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. What is the smallest integer $k$ such that any selection of $k$ points from the grid contains a set of $m+1$ points with all distinct row indices and all distinct column indices?

exact.text: \text{Žan wrote four positive real numbers } a, b, c, d \text{ such that } a = 3, d = 9. \text{ Additionally, } a, b, c \text{ form a geometric progression, and } b, c, d \text{ form an arithmetic progression. Find the values of } a, b, c, d.

paraphrase.text: A sequence of four positive real numbers is given such that the initial term is $3$ and the final term is $9$. The first three numbers are in geometric progression, while the last three are in arithmetic progression. Find all four numbers in the sequence.

exact.text: Let $\lfloor a \rfloor$ denote the floor function for any real number $a$. Determine all integers $y$ such that there exists a real number $x$ satisfying $\lfloor \frac{x+23}{8} \rfloor = \lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor = y$.

style.text: Suppose $m$ is a positive integer such that $m^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{5}$. Prove that $m^2 - 1$ can be expressed as the sum of five perfect squares.

exact.text:
Let $a 
eq 0$ be a real number. Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{R} 	o \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$
f(x+y) + f(x)f(y) = axy
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

paraphrase.text: Let $c \neq 0$ be a real number. Find all functions $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $$ g(p)g(q) + g(p+q) = cpq $$ holds for all real numbers $p$ and $q$.

style.text:
Let $b 
eq 0$ be a real number. Find all functions $g : \mathbb{R} 	o \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
g(p)g(q) + g(p+q) = bpq
$$
for all real numbers $p$ and $q$.

paraphrase.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer and $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of ordered $n$-tuples of real numbers. Let $S$ denote the collection of $(y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ for which there exists a bijection $\tau$ from $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ to itself such that $y_{\tau(i)} - y_{\tau(i+1)} \ge 1$ for all $1 \le i < n$. Show that there exists a real number $d$ such that for any $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, one can find $(b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n)$, $(c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n) \in S$ with $$ a_i = \frac{1}{2}(b_i + c_i), \quad |a_i - b_i| \le d, \quad |a_i - c_i| \le d \quad (1 \le i \le n). $$

style.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer and consider the set $S$ of all $n$-tuples $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that there exists a reordering $\pi$ of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for which $x_{\pi(1)} - x_{\pi(2)} \ge 1$, $x_{\pi(2)} - x_{\pi(3)} \ge 1$, and so on until $x_{\pi(n-1)} - x_{\pi(n)} \ge 1$. Prove that there exists a constant $d$ such that for any $n$-tuple $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, there exist $n$-tuples $(b_1, \dots, b_n), (c_1, \dots, c_n) \in S$ such that $a_i = \frac{1}{2}(b_i + c_i)$, and $|a_i - b_i|, |a_i - c_i| \le d$ for all $1 \le i \le n$.

exact.text:
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be the side lengths of a triangle with inradius $r$. Show that
$$
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{1}{a^2} \le \frac{1}{4r^2}.
$$

paraphrase.text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ denote the sides of a triangle and let $r$ be the inradius. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{x^2} + \frac{1}{y^2} + \frac{1}{z^2} \le \frac{1}{4r^2}.
$$

style.text: \text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be the side lengths of a triangle with inradius } r. \text{ Prove that} \quad \frac{1}{x^2} + \frac{1}{y^2} + \frac{1}{z^2} \le \frac{1}{4r^2}.

exact.text: Determine the maximum value of $ t $ such that, for any school with $ 2006 $ students and $ 14 $ teachers where each student is connected to at least one teacher, there exists a student-teacher pair who are connected, and the quotient of the number of students connected to the teacher and the number of teachers connected to the student is no less than $ t $.

paraphrase.text: Determine the maximum real number $ t $ such that, for any configuration of $ 2006 $ students and $ 14 $ teachers in a school where each student is connected to at least one teacher, there exists a student-teacher pair who are connected, and the ratio of the number of students connected to the teacher to the number of teachers connected to the student is at least $ t $.

style.text: Determine the maximum real number $ t $ such that, in any setup with $ 2006 $ individuals labeled as students and $ 14 $ labeled as mentors, where each student is connected to at least one mentor, there exists a pair consisting of a student and a mentor who are connected, and the ratio of the number of students connected to the mentor to the number of mentors connected to the student is at least $ t $.

exact.text: Given a graph $G$ with $n = 30$ vertices and $m = 105$ edges, if the number of unordered pairs of edges that are non-adjacent is $4822$, determine the maximum possible difference between the degrees of two vertices in $G$. (Azer Kerimov).

paraphrase.text: In a graph $G$ with $30$ nodes and $105$ connections, there are $4822$ unordered pairs of connections that do not share a common node. Determine the largest possible difference between the degrees of two nodes in the graph.

style.text: In a graph $G$ with $30$ nodes and $105$ connections, the count of unordered pairs of disjoint connections (edges that do not share an endpoint) is $4822$. Determine the largest possible difference between the degrees of any two nodes.

exact.text: A $2007 \times 2007$ grid has some squares marked. For each marked square $(i, j)$, define $S_{i,j}$ as the set of all marked squares $(x, y)$ such that $x \leq i$ and $y \leq j$. Initially, in each marked square $(i, j)$, write the cardinality of $S_{i,j}$. Then, in each subsequent step, in each marked square $(i, j)$, write the sum of all numbers written in $S_{i,j}$ from the previous step. Prove that after some finite number of steps, all written numbers in the marked squares will be odd.

paraphrase.text: Let a $2007 \times 2007$ grid have some squares marked as special. For each square $(i, j)$, define $T_{i,j}$ to be the set of all special squares $(x, y)$ such that $x \leq i$ and $y \leq j$. At the first stage, in each special square $(i, j)$, we place the count of special squares in $T_{i,j}$. In each subsequent stage, in each special square $(i, j)$, we place the sum of all numbers in $T_{i,j}$ from the previous stage. Show that after a finite number of stages, all numbers in the special squares will be odd.

style.text: Some cells of a $2007 \times 2007$ grid are marked. For any marked cell $(i, j)$, define $T_{i,j}$ as the set of all marked cells $(x, y)$ such that $x \leq i$ and $y \leq j$. In the first step, each marked cell $(i, j)$ is assigned the count of marked cells in $T_{i,j}$. In each subsequent step, each marked cell $(i, j)$ is assigned the sum of all values from $T_{i,j}$ computed in the previous step. Prove that after finitely many steps, all values in the marked cells are odd.

exact.text: In a country, there are $2010$ cities each directly connected to the capital via a highway. For any city (other than the capital), the number of direct connections is strictly less than $2010$, and if two cities have the same number of connections, that number is even. Suppose $k$ of the highways from the capital are to be closed for maintenance. Determine the largest possible value of $k$ such that the road network remains fully connected regardless of the original configuration of the network.

paraphrase.text: A country has $2010$ cities directly connected to the capital by road. For any non-capital city, the number of other cities it is connected to is strictly less than $2010$, and if two non-capital cities have the same degree, that degree is even. Suppose $k$ highways from the capital are to be shut down for maintenance. Determine the largest possible value of $k$ such that road connectivity is preserved in the country for any configuration of the network.

style.text: A network of $2010$ nodes is connected to a central hub. Each other node has fewer than $2010$ connections, and if two nodes have the same number of connections, that number is even. $k$ connections from the hub to the other nodes will be removed. Determine the largest $k$ such that the network remains connected, regardless of how it was originally constructed.

exact.text: In a bipartite graph with two sets each of $2011$ vertices, each edge is labeled by one of at most $19$ different colors assigned to each vertex. Determine the largest integer $k$ such that no matter how the edges are labeled, there is a monochromatic connected subgraph involving at least $k$ vertices.

paraphrase.text: In a complete bipartite graph $K_{2011,2011}$, each edge is assigned to one of at most $19$ labels at each vertex. Determine the maximum integer $k$ such that for any such assignment, there exists a monochromatic connected subgraph containing at least $k$ vertices.

style.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be two disjoint sets of $2011$ elements each. Every pair $x \in X$, $y \in Y$ is connected by a unique edge labeled with a color. Each vertex is incident to at most $19$ different colors. Determine the maximum integer $k$ such that in any such coloring, there exists a monochromatic connected subgraph with at least $k$ vertices.

paraphrase.text:
Let $a < b$ be positive integers and $q = \frac{b^2 + a^2}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}$.
\na. Find three pairs of positive integers $(a, b)$ for which $q$ is a prime number.
\nb. Prove that if $q$ is a prime number, then $q \equiv 1 \pmod 8$.

exact.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets with $|A| = 2011^2$ and $|B| = 2010$. Prove that there exists a symmetric function $f: A \times A \to B$ such that for any mapping $g: A \to B$, there are distinct elements $a_1, a_2 \in A$ with $g(a_1) = f(a_1, a_2) = g(a_2)$.

paraphrase.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets with $2011^2$ and $2010$ elements, respectively. Prove that there exists a symmetric function $f: X \times X \to Y$ such that for any mapping $h: X \to Y$, there exist distinct elements $x_1, x_2 \in X$ satisfying $h(x_1) = f(x_1, x_2) = h(x_2)$.

style.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets such that $|X| = 2011^2$ and $|Y| = 2010$. Prove that there exists a symmetric function $f: X \times X \to Y$ with the property that for every mapping $h: X \to Y$, there exist distinct elements $x_1, x_2 \in X$ such that $h(x_1) = f(x_1, x_2) = h(x_2)$.

exact.text: In triangle $ABC$, let $I$ be the incenter and $D$ be the point where the incircle touches $BC$. Define $T$ as the midpoint of $ID$. Let $K$ and $L$ be the intersections of the line through $I$ perpendicular to $AD$ with $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $M$ and $N$ be the intersections of the line through $T$ perpendicular to $AD$ with $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Prove that $KM \cdot LN = BM \cdot CN$.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$, and suppose the incircle touches side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $T$ be the midpoint of segment $ID$. A line through $I$ perpendicular to $AD$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively. A line through $T$ perpendicular to $AD$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $M$ and $N$, respectively. Prove that $KM \cdot LN = BM \cdot CN$.

style.text: Let $PQR$ be a triangle with incenter $J$, and let the incircle touch $QR$ at point $S$. Let $U$ be the midpoint of segment $JS$. A line through $J$ perpendicular to $PS$ intersects $PQ$ and $PR$ at points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. A line through $U$ perpendicular to $PS$ intersects $PQ$ and $PR$ at points $Z$ and $W$, respectively. Prove that $XZ \cdot YW = QZ \cdot RW$.

exact.text: Determine all positive integers $n$ such that $\frac{n! - 1}{2n + 7}$ is an integer.

paraphrase.text: Determine all positive integers $n$ such that $n! - 1$ is divisible by $2n + 7$.

style.text: Determine all positive integers $ m $ such that $ 2m + 7 $ divides $ m! - 1 $.

exact.text:
Prove that for all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ with $x + y + z = 1$, the inequality below holds:
$$
\frac{x^4 + 5y^4}{x(x + 2y)} + \frac{y^4 + 5z^4}{y(y + 2z)} + \frac{z^4 + 5x^4}{z(z + 2x)} \ge 1 - xy - yz - zx
$$

paraphrase.text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{x^4 + 5y^4}{x(x + 2y)} + \frac{y^4 + 5z^4}{y(y + 2z)} + \frac{z^4 + 5x^4}{z(z + 2x)} \ge 1 - xy - yz - zx.
$$

style.text:
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z = 1$. Prove the inequality:
$$
\frac{x^4 + 5y^4}{x(x + 2y)} + \frac{y^4 + 5z^4}{y(y + 2z)} + \frac{z^4 + 5x^4}{z(z + 2x)} \ge 1 - xy - yz - zx
$$

exact.text: In a country with $100$ cities, $2013$ round trip flights are operated by $n$ airlines. It is known that there are at least two cities that cannot be reached from each other using at most two flights. However, for every pair of cities, there exists at least one airline whose flights (direct or indirect) connect them. What is the largest possible value of $n$?

paraphrase.text: In a country with $100$ cities, $2013$ round trip flights connect certain pairs of cities. These flights are operated by $n$ different airlines. It is known that there exist two cities such that neither is reachable from the other by at most two flights. However, for any pair of cities, there exists a sequence of flights (possibly multiple) operated by a single airline that connects them. Determine the maximum possible value of $n$.

style.text: A network of $100$ towns is connected by $2013$ bidirectional roads managed by $n$ different construction firms. There exist at least two towns such that the distance between them is greater than $2$. However, for every pair of towns, there is at least one firm whose roads connect them directly or indirectly. Determine the largest possible value of $n$.

exact.text: A tournament is held among $2017$ participants where each pair plays at most one game. It is given that for any pair of participants who played each other, at least one of them has played at most $22$ games in total. What is the largest number of games that could have been played in the tournament?

paraphrase.text: In a competition with $2017$ participants, each pair of participants played at most one game. It was observed that for any two participants who played a game, at least one of them had played no more than $22$ games overall. Determine the maximum number of games that could have been played in the competition.

style.text: In a math competition among $2017$ participants, each pair competed at most once. It was observed that whenever two participants had a match, at least one of them had participated in at most $22$ matches. What is the maximum number of matches that could have been played in the competition?

exact.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $BC \nparallel AD$. Let $E$ lie inside the circumcircle of $ABCD$ on the side of $AB$ opposite to $C$. The intersection of $DE$ and $AB$ is $F$. Let $G$ be a point inside $ABCD$ lying on the tangent at $E$ to the circumcircle of $\triangle AEF$. If $$ \angle GAD = \angle BAF \text{ and } \angle GCB + \angle GBA = \angle EAD + \angle AGD + \angle ABE $$ show that the lines $BC$, $AD$, and $EG$ meet at a single point.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $BC$ and $AD$ not parallel. Let $E$ lie inside the circumcircle of $ABCD$ such that it is on the opposite side of $AB$ relative to $C$. Let $F$ be the intersection of $DE$ and $AB$. Let $G$ lie inside $ABCD$ on the tangent at $E$ to the circumcircle of triangle $AEF$. If $$\angle DAG = \angle FAB \text{ and } \angle GBA + \angle GCB = \angle AED + \angle AGD + \angle AEB$$ then prove that $BC$, $AD$, and $EG$ are concurrent.

style.text: Let $PQRS$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $RS$ and $PQ$ not parallel. Let $T$ be a point inside the circumcircle of $PQRS$ on the opposite side of the line $PQ$ with respect to point $R$. The lines $ST$ and $PQ$ intersect at $U$. Let $V$ be a point inside $PQRS$ and on the line tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $PTU$ at $T$. If $$\angle VPS = \angle QPU \text{ and } \angle VSR + \angle VQP = \angle TSP + \angle VSP + \angle PTU$$ then show that the lines $RS$, $PQ$ and $TV$ are concurrent.

exact.text: Given positive integers $x$ and $y$, prove that there exists a positive integer $m$ such that $m^2 + xm + y$ is divisible by at least $2018$ different primes.

paraphrase.text: Prove that for every two positive integers $(c, d)$, there exists a positive integer $m$ such that the quadratic expression $m^2 + cm + d$ possesses at least $2018$ different prime factors.

style.text: Prove that for any positive integers $x$ and $y$, there exists a positive integer $m$ such that the expression $m^2 + xm + y$ is divisible by at least $2018$ different primes.

exact.text: A point $(x, y)$ on the plane is called *primitive* if $x, y$ are integers with $\gcd(x, y) = 1$. A graph is defined with primitive points as vertices. An edge is added between $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ if and only if $2x_1 = 2x_2 = y_1 - y_2$ or $2x_1 = 2x_2 = y_2 - y_1$ or $2y_1 = 2y_2 = x_1 - x_2$ or $2y_1 = 2y_2 = x_2 - x_1$. After removing some edges to make the graph a forest, what is the minimum number of edges that must be removed? What is the minimum number of trees in the resulting forest?

paraphrase.text: Let $P = (x, y)$ be a point with integer coordinates and $\gcd(x, y) = 1$. Define a graph with such points as vertices and an edge between $P = (x_1, y_1)$ and $Q = (x_2, y_2)$ if and only if $2x_1 = 2x_2 = |y_1 - y_2|$ or $2y_1 = 2y_2 = |x_1 - x_2|$. If edges are removed until the graph becomes a forest, what is the minimum number of edges to be removed? What is the minimum number of trees that can be in the resulting forest?

style.text: Let $P$ be a point $(x, y)$ with integer coordinates and $\gcd(x, y) = 1$. A graph is defined on all such $P$ by connecting two points $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ with an edge if and only if $2x_1 = 2x_2 = |y_1 - y_2|$ or $2y_1 = 2y_2 = |x_1 - x_2|$. Suppose edges are removed until the graph becomes a forest. What is the minimum number of edges that must be removed? What is the minimum number of trees in the resulting forest?

exact.text: There are $n$ stone piles each with $2018$ stones. Each stone has a weight from $\{1, 2, \ldots, 25\}$, and all pile total weights are distinct. If two piles are selected and the lightest and heaviest stones are removed from each, the previously heavier pile becomes the lighter one. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

paraphrase.text: There are $n$ stone stacks each containing $2018$ stones. Each stone has a weight from $1$ to $25$, and all stack weights are distinct. If we take any two stacks and remove the maximum and minimum stones from each, the previously heavier stack becomes the lighter one. Find the maximum possible value of $n$.

style.text: There are $n$ bags each containing $2018$ pebbles. Each pebble has a weight in the range $1$ to $25$. The total weights of the bags are all distinct. Moreover, for any two bags, if we remove the heaviest and the lightest pebble from each, the previously heavier bag becomes the lighter one. What is the maximum possible value of $n$?

exact.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer with $b$ digits and $l, r$ be non-negative integers such that $l + r < b$. A positive integer is a sub-divisor of $n$ if it divides the number formed by removing the first $l$ and the last $r$ digits of $n$. Let $A_d$ denote the set of all positive integers for which $d$ is not a sub-divisor. Determine all values of $d$ such that $A_d$ is finite.

paraphrase.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer with $b$ digits and $l, r$ be non-negative integers such that $l + r < b$. A positive integer $d$ is called a sub-divisor of $n$ if there exist $l, r$ such that $d$ divides the number formed by deleting the first $l$ and last $r$ digits of $n$. Define $A_d$ as the set of all positive integers $n$ for which $d$ is not a sub-divisor of $n$. Determine all positive integers $d$ for which $A_d$ is a finite set.

style.text: Let $m$ be a number with $k$ digits and $p, q$ be non-negative integers such that $p + q < k$. A positive integer is called a segment-divisor of $m$ if it divides the number formed by removing the first $p$ and last $q$ digits of $m$. (For instance, segment-divisors of $143$ are $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $7$, $11$, $13$, $14$, $43$ and $143$.) For each positive integer $d$, define $B_d$ as the set of numbers for which $d$ is not a segment-divisor. Determine all $d$ for which $B_d$ is finite.

exact.text:
Let $\sigma(n)$ be the total number of positive divisors of $n$ and $s(n)$ the number of divisors $d$ of $n$ for which $d+1$ divides $n+1$. Determine the maximum value of
$$
2s(n) - \sigma(n).
$$

paraphrase.text: Let $f(n)$ be the number of positive divisors of $n$ and $g(n)$ be the number of positive divisors $d$ of $n$ for which $d+1$ divides $n+1$. Determine the maximum value of $2g(n) - f(n)$ over all positive integers $n$.

style.text:
For any positive integer $ m $, define $ f(m) $ to be the number of positive divisors $ k $ of $ m $ such that $ k - 1 $ divides $ m - 1 $. Let $ g(m) $ be the total number of positive divisors of $ m $. Determine the maximum possible value of
$$
2f(m) - g(m).
$$

exact.text:
Let $x, y, z, w$ be positive integers such that any circular arrangement of these numbers includes at least one pair of adjacent non-coprime numbers. Determine the maximum number of distinct ordered triples $(p, q, r)$; $p, q, r \in \{x, y, z, w\}$, $p 
eq q, q 
eq r, r 
eq p$, such that $(	ext{gcd}(p, q))^2 \mid r$.

paraphrase.text: Let $x, y, z, w$ be positive integers such that in every circular permutation of these numbers, there are two adjacent elements with a common factor greater than 1. Determine the largest possible count of ordered triples $(p, q, r)$; $p, q, r \in \{x, y, z, w\}$, with distinct $p, q, r$, satisfying $(\gcd(p, q))^2 \mid r$.

style.text: Let $x, y, z, w$ be positive integers such that any cyclic permutation of these numbers contains at least one pair of adjacent numbers with a common factor greater than 1. What is the maximum number of ordered triples $(p, q, r)$; $p, q, r \in \{x, y, z, w\}$ and distinct, such that $(\gcd(p, q))^2$ divides $r$?

exact.text: We have two containers: one with $29$ distinct items and one empty. In each move, we transfer a non-empty subset of items from the chosen container to the other. We begin with the non-empty container and alternate the choice of container each turn. What is the maximum number of such moves if each subset can be used at most once?

paraphrase.text: Two containers hold $29$ distinct items initially in one and the other being empty. In each move, a container is selected, and a non-empty subset of its contents is moved to the other container. The moves alternate between the containers, starting with the one that is not empty. What is the greatest number of such moves possible, assuming each subset is used at most once?

style.text: Two containers are labeled $A$ and $B$. Initially, container $A$ holds $29$ distinct tokens and $B$ is empty. In a move, you choose a non-empty subset of the current container and move it to the other. You must alternate containers: first from $A$, then from $B$, and so on. What is the maximum number of such moves if no subset is reused?

exact.text: In triangle $ABC$, the circle $\omega$ with diameter $BC$ is tangent to the external angle bisector of $\angle A$. The internal angle bisector of $\angle A$ intersects $BC$ at $K$ and the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $L \neq A$. If $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, prove that the circumcircle of triangle $KLM$ is tangent to $\omega$.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that the circle $\omega$ with diameter $BC$ is tangent to the external bisector of $\angle BAC$. The internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets $BC$ at point $K$ and intersects the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ again at point $L$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $BC$. Prove that the circle passing through $K$, $L$, and $M$ is tangent to $\omega$.

style.text: In triangle $XYZ$, let $\omega$ be the circle with diameter $YZ$ that is tangent to the external bisector of $\angle YXZ$. The internal angle bisector of $\angle YXZ$ meets $YZ$ at point $P$ and the circumcircle of $XYZ$ at point $Q \ne X$. Let $N$ be the midpoint of $YZ$. Prove that the circumcircle of $NPQ$ is tangent to $\omega$.

exact.text: Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ lie on a semicircle with diameter $XY$. The tangents at $A$ and $B$ meet the line $XY$ at $M$ and $N$, respectively. A vertical line through $A$ intersects $NC$ at $R$, and a vertical line through $B$ intersects $MC$ at $S$. The segment $RS$ intersects $XY$ at $Z$. Prove that $ZC$ is tangent to the semicircle.

paraphrase.text: Points $P$, $Q$, $R$ lie on a semicircle. The tangent to the semicircle at $P$ meets the diameter at $S$, and the tangent at $Q$ meets the diameter at $T$. A line through $P$ perpendicular to the diameter intersects $TR$ at $U$, and a line through $Q$ perpendicular to the diameter intersects $SR$ at $V$. The segment $UV$ intersects the diameter at $W$. Prove that $WR$ is tangent to the semicircle.

style.text: Let a semicircle with diameter $XY$ contain points $P$, $Q$, and $T$. The tangent at $P$ intersects $XY$ at $U$, and the tangent at $Q$ intersects $XY$ at $V$. A vertical line through $P$ intersects $VT$ at $R$, and a vertical line through $Q$ intersects $UT$ at $S$. The segment $RS$ meets $XY$ at $W$. Prove that $WT$ is tangent to the semicircle.

exact.text:
Find all pairs $(a, b)$ of prime numbers such that
$$
2^a = 2^{b-2} + b!
$$

paraphrase.text:
Determine all prime number pairs $(r, s)$ such that
$$
2^r = 2^{s-2} + s!
$$

style.text: \text{Determine all prime number pairs } (a, b) \text{ such that } 2^a = 2^{b-2} + b!.

exact.text:
Determine the maximum value of $x - y$, given that $x$, $y$, $z$ are real numbers such that
$$
 x + y + z = 2, \quad xy + yz + zx = 1.
$$

paraphrase.text: Determine the maximum value of $a - b$, where $a$, $b$, $c$ are real numbers such that $a + b + c = 2$ and $ab + bc + ca = 1$.

style.text: Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be real numbers such that $a + b + c = 2$ and $ab + bc + ca = 1$. Find the maximum value of $a - b$.

exact.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $K$ on $AC$ and $L$ on $BC$ such that $\angle AKB = \angle ALB$. Let $P = AL \cap BK$ and $Q$ be the midpoint of $KL$. Let $T = AL \cap \omega$, $S = BK \cap \omega$, where $\omega$ is the circumcircle of $ABC$. Prove that the lines $TK, SL, PQ$ meet at a common point.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with points $K, L$ lying on $AC$ and $BC$ respectively, satisfying $\angle AKB = \angle ALB$. Let $P$ denote the intersection point of $AL$ and $BK$, and let $Q$ be the midpoint of $KL$. Let $T$ and $S$ be the second points where $AL$ and $BK$ meet the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Show that the lines $TK$, $SL$, and $PQ$ are concurrent.

style.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, points $K$ and $L$ lie on $AC$ and $BC$ respectively with $\angle AKB = \angle ALB$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of lines $BK$ and $AL$, and let $Q$ be the midpoint of segment $KL$. Let $T$ and $S$ be the second intersections of lines $AL$ and $BK$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Prove that lines $TK$, $SL$, and $PQ$ are concurrent.

exact.text: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, and orthocenter $H$. Consider the circle through $O$ tangent to $IH$ at $I$ and the circle through $H$ tangent to $IO$ at $I$. Let these circles intersect at $I$ and another point $M$. Prove that $M$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

paraphrase.text: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, and orthocenter $H$. Consider the circle through $O$ tangent to $IH$ at $I$, and the circle through $H$ tangent to $IO$ at $I$. Let their second point of intersection be $M$. Prove that $M$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

style.text: In triangle $PQR$, let $G$ be the circumcenter, $K$ be the incenter, and $T$ be the orthocenter. Let $S$ be the second intersection point of the circle through $G$ tangent to $TK$ at $K$ and the circle through $T$ tangent to $KG$ at $K$. Prove that $S$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $PQR$.

exact.text: Let $K_{2024}$ be a complete graph with all its edges assigned one of 13 distinct labels. If it is always possible to select $k$ labels such that the subgraph formed by edges with those labels is connected, find the smallest such $k$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose the edges of the complete graph $K_{2024}$ are assigned one of 13 different labels. It is guaranteed that for any such assignment, there exists a subset of $k$ labels such that the subgraph consisting of edges with those labels is connected. Determine the smallest possible value of $k$.

style.text: Suppose all the connections in a fully connected network of 2024 nodes are assigned one of 13 distinct labels. It is guaranteed that, no matter how the connections are assigned, there exists a set of $k$ labels such that the network remains connected when only connections with those labels are considered. Determine the smallest such $k$.

exact.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral. Let the incenters of triangles $BAD$ and $CAD$ be denoted by $I$ and $J$, respectively. If $L$ is the intersection of the line through $I$ perpendicular to $BD$ and the line through $J$ perpendicular to $AC$, show that $LI = LJ$.

paraphrase.text: Suppose $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Denote by $I$ and $J$ the incenters of triangles $ABD$ and $ACD$, respectively. Let $K$ be the point of intersection of the perpendicular from $I$ to diagonal $BD$ and the perpendicular from $J$ to diagonal $AC$. Prove that the distances $KI$ and $KJ$ are equal.

style.text: Let $PQRS$ be a cyclic quadrilateral, and let the incenters of triangles $PQS$ and $PRS$ be $M$ and $N$, respectively. Let the intersection point of the line through $M$ perpendicular to $QS$ and the line through $N$ perpendicular to $PR$ be $T$. Prove that $TM = TN$.

exact.text:
設 $n$ 為大於 2 的正偶數，實數 $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ 滿足
$$
\sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} (a_i - a_j)^2 = 1.
$$
試求 $\sum_{k=1}^{n} (a_k - a_{k+1})^2$ 的最大值，其中 $a_{n+1} = a_1$。

paraphrase.text:
設 $n > 2$ 是偶數，且實數 $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ 滿足

\sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} (a_i - a_j)^2 = 1.
$$
試求 $\sum_{i=1}^{n} (a_i - a_{i+1})^2$ 的最大值，其中 $a_{n+1} = a_1$。

style.text: 令 $n$ 為大於 2 的偶數，設實數 $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ 滿足 $$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le n} (a_i - a_j)^2 = 1.$$ 試求 $$\sum_{k=1}^{n} (a_k - a_{k+1})^2$$ 的最大值，其中 $a_{n+1} = a_1$。

exact.text: 設 $P(x)$ 是一個次數不超過 $n$ 的多項式, 且 $P(0), P(1), \dots, P(n)$ 這 $n+1$ 個值中, 任意兩值之差皆為整數。試證: $P(2011) - P(100)$ 也是整數。

exact.text:
有65對情侶出去玩，每位男生都有一輛機車，並載一位女生。假設存在一種安排，使得對任意兩輛機車，下面兩者恰好其一為真：
(i) 兩輛機車上的男生彼此認識；
(ii) 兩輛機車上的女生的男朋友彼此認識。
試證：存在一對情侶，若將他們剔除，則剩餘的64對情侶仍能安排出符合上述條件的載法。

paraphrase.text:
假設有65對夫婦一起騎機車出遊,每對夫婦中丈夫都騎機車載妻子。現有一種安排方式,使得對任意兩輛機車,以下兩種情形恰有一種成立:
(i) 兩位機車駕駛互相認識;
(ii) 兩位乘客的丈夫互相認識。
試證明:存在一對夫婦,剔除後剩下的64對夫婦仍可安排出一個滿足上述條件的載法。

style.text:
有65組朋友結伴旅行，每組都包含一名男生和一名女生。每位男生都有一輛摩托車，並負責載一名女生。假設他們能找到一種載人方式，使得對於任意兩輛摩托車，下面兩種情形恰有一種成立：
(i) 兩輛摩托車上的男生互相認識；
(ii) 兩輛摩托車上的女生的男朋友互相認識。
試證明：一定能找到一組朋友，剔除他們後，剩下64組仍能安排出一種符合上述條件的載人方式。

exact.text: 設 $f$ 和 $g$ 是整係數的非零多項式, 且 $\deg f > \deg g$。若存在無限多個質數 $p$ 使得 $pf + g$ 有一個有理根, 試證 $f$ 有一個有理根。

exact.text:
考慮一個 $3n \times 3n$ 的棋盤，其行與列皆由 1 到 $3n$ 進行標號。若 $(x + y) \mod 3 = 0$、$1$、$2$，則方格 $(x, y)$ 分別塗成顏色 A、B、C。每個格子內有一個顏色為 A、B 或 C 的籌碼，且每種顏色的籌碼數目皆為 $3n^2$。
若存在一種重新排列方法，使得顏色 A 被顏色 B 取代、顏色 B 被顏色 C 取代、顏色 C 被顏色 A 取代，且每個籌碼移動距離不超過 $d$，則試證：存在另一種重新排列方式，使得每個籌碼移動距離不超過 $d+2$，且每個格子內的籌碼顏色與該格子的顏色一致。

paraphrase.text: 設 $3n \times 3n$ 的棋盤中，方格 $(x, y)$ 的顏色依 $x + y \mod 3$ 的值為 0, 1, 2 時分別為 A, B, C。在每個方格中放入一個顏色為 A, B 或 C 的籌碼，且每種顏色各有 $3n^2$ 個。若存在一種排列方式，使得顏色 A 的籌碼取代顏色 B 的籌碼、顏色 B 的籌碼取代顏色 C 的籌碼、顏色 C 的籌碼取代顏色 A 的籌碼，且每個籌碼移動距離不超過 $d$，試證存在另一種排列方式，使得每個籌碼移動距離不超過 $d+2$，且最終每個方格的顏色與其內的籌碼一致。

style.text:
考慮一個 $3n \times 3n$ 的棋盤，其方格 $(x, y)$ 按 $x + y$ 除以 3 的餘數被標記為顏色 R, G, B。每種顏色的方格數目相同。在每個方格中放一個標記，標記顏色為 R, G, B 之一，且三種顏色的標記各有 $3n^2$ 個。
現已知一種排列方式，使得 R 位置被 G 取代，G 被 B 取代，B 被 R 取代，且每標記移動距離不超過 $d$。證明：存在另一種排列方式，使得每個標記移動距離不超過 $d + 2$，且最終每個方格的標記顏色與該方格本身顏色相同。

exact.text: 令 $x$ 和 $y$ 是正整數。試證若對所有的正整數 $n$, $2^n y + 1$ 整除 $x \cdot 2^n - 1$, 則 $x = 1$。

paraphrase.text: 設 $a$ 和 $b$ 是正整數。證明若對所有正整數 $n$, $2^n b + 1$ 整除 $a 2^n - 1$, 則 $a = 1$。

exact.text:
A physicist discovered a new kind of particle, called an imon, which can form entanglements with others. He can perform two operations:
(1) If an imon is entangled with an odd number of others, he can remove it.
(2) He can duplicate all imons, such that for each imon $I$, a new imon $I'$ is created. The new imons $I'$ and $J'$ are entangled if and only if the original $I$ and $J$ are entangled, and each $I'$ is entangled with $I$. No other entanglements are created.
Show that the physicist can perform a sequence of these operations to obtain a set of imons with no entanglements between them.

paraphrase.text:
A physicist is studying entangled particles known as imons. Each imon may be entangled with many others. The physicist can perform the following operations:
(1) If an imon is entangled with an odd number of others, it can be removed.
(2) The physicist can create a duplicate of every imon, such that the duplicate $I'$ of imon $I$ becomes entangled with $J'$ if and only if $I$ was entangled with $J$, and also with $I$. No other entanglements are introduced.
Show that it is possible to perform a sequence of such operations to end up with a set of imons with no entanglements among them.

style.text:
A scientist in a quantum lab discovers a collection of particles called quarks. These quarks can form quark pairs; each quark can be in many such pairs. The scientist has access to two operations:
(1) If a quark is paired with an odd number of other quarks, the scientist can remove it.
(2) The scientist can duplicate the entire system of quarks. For each quark $Q$, a copy $Q'$ is created. The copy $Q'$ forms a pair with $R'$ if and only if the original quarks $Q$ and $R$ were paired; also, $Q'$ forms a pair with $Q$. No other pairings are created.
Prove that it is possible for the scientist to perform a sequence of these operations and end up with a group of quarks such that no two are paired.

exact.text: In a country with a connected network of cities and bidirectional flights, define the distance between two cities as the minimum number of flights required to travel between them. Suppose every city has no more than 100 cities at a distance of precisely 3. Show that no city can have more than 2550 cities at distance exactly 4 from it.

The *distance* between two vertices is the minimum number of edges in a path connecting them. Suppose that for every vertex, there are at most 100 vertices at distance exactly 3 from it. Prove that no vertex has more than 2550 vertices at distance exactly 4 from it.

style.text: In a connected graph, each vertex is connected to other vertices by edges. The distance between two vertices is the length of the shortest path connecting them. It is given that for any vertex, there are at most 100 vertices at distance exactly three from it. Prove that no vertex has more than 2550 vertices at distance exactly four from it.
